Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 28, verses 1–6:

[In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. My Lord, make it easy by Your grace.] [[Addition from T.]]

TAFSIR (exegesis) OF SURAH AL-QASAS (THE STORIES)

[It is Meccan.] [[Addition from F.]]

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Ishaq, from Ma'd Yakrib, who said: "We came to Abdullah and asked him to recite to us Ta, Sin, Mim (the two hundreds). He said: 'I do not have them with me, but go to the one among you who took them from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): Khabbab ibn al-Aratt.' He said: So we came to Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, and he recited them to us, may Allah be pleased with him." [[Al-Musnad (1/419).]]

* *

The discussion of the disjointed letters has already preceded.

* *

His saying: ﴿These are the verses of the Clear Book﴾, that is, these are the verses of the Book that is manifest, clear, revealing the realities of matters and the knowledge of what has occurred and what will occur.

* *

His saying: ﴿We recite to you some of the news of Musa and Fir'awn in truth, for a people who believe﴾, as the Exalted said: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories﴾ [Yusuf: 3], that is, We mention to you the matter as it was, as if you were witnessing it and as if you were present.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, Fir'awn exalted himself in the land﴾, that is, he was arrogant, tyrannical and transgressed. ﴿And made its people into factions﴾, that is, into groups, having directed each group toward what he wished of the affairs of his state.

* *

His saying: ﴿He oppressed a group among them﴾ refers to the Children of Israel. At that time they were the best people of their era. Despite this, this tyrannical, obstinate king had power over them, employing them in the most degrading work, driving them night and day in his tasks and the tasks of his subjects. Along with this, he would kill their sons and spare their women, as humiliation and contempt for them, and out of fear that there would be found among them the boy whom he and the people of his kingdom had feared would be found, the one who would be the cause of his destruction and the ending of his rule at his hands. The Copts had taken this from the Children of Israel, from what they used to study of the saying of Ibrahim the Friend (al-Khalil), when he entered the land of Egypt and what happened to him with its tyrant occurred, when he took Sarah to make her a slave-girl. Allah protected her from him and prevented him from her by His power and authority. Ibrahim, peace be upon him, had given good news to his son that from his loins and offspring there would be born one who would bring about the destruction of the king of Egypt at his hands. So the Copts kept speaking of this in the presence of Fir'awn, and Fir'awn took precautions against it and ordered the killing of the male children of the Children of Israel. But no precaution avails against destiny, for when the appointed term of Allah comes, it is not delayed, and for every term there is a Book. Therefore He said: ﴿And We wished to bestow favour upon those who were oppressed in the land, and to make them leaders and to make them the inheritors, and to establish them in the land, and to show Fir'awn and Haman and their hosts from them that which they were fearing﴾. And the Exalted did this with them, as He said: ﴿And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed, and the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of their patience, and We destroyed what Fir'awn and his people had been constructing and what they had been erecting﴾ [Al-A'raf: 137]. And He said: ﴿Thus, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit it﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 59]. Fir'awn, by his strength and power, wished to escape from Musa, but that did not benefit him against the decree of the Great King, whose command is not opposed by any predestination. Rather, His judgment was executed and His pen had run in eternity that the destruction of Fir'awn would be at the hands of this boy whom you feared the existence of, and for whose sake you killed thousands of infants. He would be raised and nurtured on your bed, in your house, his food from your table, while you raise him, pamper him and cherish him, and your death and destruction and the destruction of your armies would be at his hands, so that you might know that the Lord of the high heavens is the Powerful, the Victorious, the Great, the Mighty, the Strong, the Severe in punishment, who does whatever He wills, and whatever He does not will does not happen.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Qasas (28), verses 7–9:

They mention that when Pharaoh killed the male children of the Children of Israel in great numbers, the Copts feared that the Children of Israel would be wiped out, so that they themselves would have to take on the heavy labour they had been doing. They said to Pharaoh: "If this situation continues, their elders will soon die, their boys will not survive, and their women cannot do the work their men do, so that burden will fall on us." So he ordered that the boys be killed in one year and spared in the next. Harun (Aaron), peace be upon him, was born in a year when the boys were spared, and Musa (Moses), peace be upon him, was born in a year when the boys were being killed. Pharaoh had men assigned to this task, and midwives who went around among the women. Whenever they saw a woman who had conceived, they recorded her name. When the time of her delivery came, only Coptic women would attend her. If the woman bore a girl, they left her and departed. If she bore a boy, those slaughterers entered with sharp, keen knives, killed him, and left, may Allah disfigure them.

When Umm Musa (the mother of Moses) became pregnant with him, peace be upon him, no signs of pregnancy appeared on her as they did on other women, and the midwives did not notice her condition. But when she gave birth to him, a boy, she was distressed and feared greatly for him, and she loved him with an exceptional love. Musa, peace be upon him, was such that no one saw him without loving him. Whoever loved him, naturally and by law, was fortunate. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And I bestowed upon you love from Me﴾ [Ta-Ha: 39]. When she was distressed about him, she was inspired in her heart, a thought was placed in her mind, and a suggestion was breathed into her soul, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We inspired to the mother of Musa: "Suckle him; then when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear or grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers."﴾

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 28, verses 10–13:

Allah the Exalted says, informing about the heart of Musa's mother when her son was cast into the sea, that it became empty (fārigh), meaning empty of everything pertaining to worldly affairs except Musa. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu 'Ubayda, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatadah, and others.

﴿Indeed, she was about to disclose him﴾, meaning: out of the intensity of her grief, sorrow and anguish, she was nearly about to reveal that a son of hers had been taken away and to tell of her condition, had Allah not strengthened her heart and given her patience. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Had We not bound fast her heart, that she might be among the believers.﴾ And she said to his sister, ﴿Follow him up﴾, meaning: she commanded her daughter, who was grown and understood what was said to her, and said to her: ﴿Follow him up﴾, meaning: follow his track, get news of him, and seek out his situation from the various parts of the town. So she went out for that purpose, ﴿and she watched him from afar, while they did not perceive﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "from a side (ʿan janab)."

Mujahid said: "﴿from afar﴾ means from a distance."

Qatadah said: "She kept looking at him as though she did not want him to notice."

This is because when Musa, peace be upon him, settled in the house of Pharaoh, and the wife of the king loved him and wanted him to remain with her, they offered him the wet-nurses who were in their house, but he would not accept the breast of any of them and refused to take anything of that kind. So they took him out to a market, perhaps they would find a woman suitable for nursing him. When she (his sister) saw him in their hands, she recognised him, but did not show that, and they did not perceive her.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We had forbidden him the wet-nurses before﴾, meaning a decreed prohibition, owing to Allah's honouring of him, protecting him from suckling any breast other than his mother's; and because Allah, glory be to Him, made that a means of his returning to his mother, so that she would nurse him while she was secure, after having been fearful. When his sister saw them perplexed about who would nurse him, she said: ﴿Shall I direct you to a household who will take charge of him for you, and who will be sincere to him?﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: When she said that, they seized her and doubted her matter, and said to her: "What makes you know their sincerity towards him and their compassion for him?" She replied: "Their sincerity towards him and their compassion for him is their desire for the king's favour and their hope for his benefit." So they let her go, and when she said that to them and was freed from their harm, they went with her to her home, and entered with him upon his mother. She gave him her breast, and he took it, and they rejoiced greatly at that. The bearer of good news went to the wife of the king, who summoned Musa's mother, treated her kindly and gave her a generous reward, while she did not know that she was his mother in reality, but because he had accepted her breast. Then Asiya asked her to stay with her and nurse him, but she refused and said: "I have a husband and children, and I cannot remain with you. But if you wish, I will nurse him in my own house." The wife of Pharaoh agreed to that, and provided for her maintenance, gifts, clothing and abundant kindness. For this reason a hadith says: "The likeness of one who works and seeks reward from Allah in his craft for good is like the mother of Musa who nurses her child and takes her wage." Whatever He wills occurs, and whatever He does not will does not occur. He who grants, for those who fear Him, relief after every distress, and a way out after every constriction.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 28, verses 10–13:

Allah the Exalted says, informing about the heart of Musa's mother when her son was cast into the sea, that it became empty (fārigh), meaning empty of everything pertaining to worldly affairs except Musa. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu 'Ubayda, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatadah, and others.

﴿Indeed, she was about to disclose him﴾, meaning: out of the intensity of her grief, sorrow and anguish, she was nearly about to reveal that a son of hers had been taken away and to tell of her condition, had Allah not strengthened her heart and given her patience. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Had We not bound fast her heart, that she might be among the believers.﴾ And she said to his sister, ﴿Follow him up﴾, meaning: she commanded her daughter, who was grown and understood what was said to her, and said to her: ﴿Follow him up﴾, meaning: follow his track, get news of him, and seek out his situation from the various parts of the town. So she went out for that purpose, ﴿and she watched him from afar, while they did not perceive﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "from a side (ʿan janab)."

Mujahid said: "﴿from afar﴾ means from a distance."

Qatadah said: "She kept looking at him as though she did not want him to notice."

This is because when Musa, peace be upon him, settled in the house of Pharaoh, and the wife of the king loved him and wanted him to remain with her, they offered him the wet-nurses who were in their house, but he would not accept the breast of any of them and refused to take anything of that kind. So they took him out to a market, perhaps they would find a woman suitable for nursing him. When she (his sister) saw him in their hands, she recognised him, but did not show that, and they did not perceive her.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We had forbidden him the wet-nurses before﴾, meaning a decreed prohibition, owing to Allah's honouring of him, protecting him from suckling any breast other than his mother's; and because Allah, glory be to Him, made that a means of his returning to his mother, so that she would nurse him while she was secure, after having been fearful. When his sister saw them perplexed about who would nurse him, she said: ﴿Shall I direct you to a household who will take charge of him for you, and who will be sincere to him?﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: When she said that, they seized her and doubted her matter, and said to her: "What makes you know their sincerity towards him and their compassion for him?" She replied: "Their sincerity towards him and their compassion for him is their desire for the king's favour and their hope for his benefit." So they let her go, and when she said that to them and was freed from their harm, they went with her to her home, and entered with him upon his mother. She gave him her breast, and he took it, and they rejoiced greatly at that. The bearer of good news went to the wife of the king, who summoned Musa's mother, treated her kindly and gave her a generous reward, while she did not know that she was his mother in reality, but because he had accepted her breast. Then Asiya asked her to stay with her and nurse him, but she refused and said: "I have a husband and children, and I cannot remain with you. But if you wish, I will nurse him in my own house." The wife of Pharaoh agreed to that, and provided for her maintenance, gifts, clothing and abundant kindness. So Musa's mother returned with her son, content and well-pleasing, Allah having changed her fear into security, in honour, dignity and abundant provision. For this reason a hadith says: "The likeness of one who works and seeks reward from Allah in his craft for good is like the mother of Musa who nurses her child and takes her wage." And between hardship and relief there was only a little: a day and a night, or thereabouts. And Allah knows best. Glory be to Him in whose hand is the affair! Whatever He wills occurs, and whatever He does not will does not occur. He who grants, for those who fear Him, relief after every distress, and a way out after every constriction.

For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So We returned him to his mother, that her eye might be comforted, and she would not grieve, and that she might know that the promise of Allah is true﴾, meaning: in His promise to her of returning him to her and making him one of the messengers. Thus, when she saw him returned to her, she was certain that he would be a messenger from among the messengers, so she treated him in his upbringing in the manner fitting for him, both by nature and by law.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 28, verse 14–17:

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the beginning of the matter of Musa, peace be upon him, He mentioned that when he reached his full strength (ashuddahu) and became mature (istawa), Allah gave him ḥukman (judgment/wisdom) and ʿilman (knowledge). Mujahid said: "It means prophethood." ﴿And thus do We reward the doers of good.﴾

Then Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the cause of his arrival at what Allah had decreed for him of prophethood and speaking directly (with Allah): the matter of his killing that Egyptian (qibti), which was the cause of his departure from the land of Egypt to the lands of Madyan. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And he entered the city at a time of unawareness of its people.﴾ Ibn Jurayj related from ʿAta' al-Khurasani, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "That was between Maghrib and ʿIsha'."

Ibn al-Munkadir related from ʿAta' ibn Yasar, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "That was at midday." Likewise said Saʿid ibn Jubayr, ʿIkrimah, al-Suddi, and Qatadah.

﴿And he found therein two men fighting,﴾ i.e., striking each other and disputing, ﴿one from his party﴾ i.e., from the Children of Israel [[In manuscript T: "i.e., an Israelite."]], ﴿and the other from his enemy﴾ i.e., a Qibti. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq. So the Israelite sought help from Musa, peace be upon him, and Musa found an opportunity, which was the people's heedlessness, so he went to the Qibti ﴿and struck him, and he died.﴾

Mujahid said: "Wakazahu" means he struck him with the full palm of his hand. Qatadah said: he struck him with a staff that he had with him.

﴿And he (Musa) put an end to him﴾ i.e., death was decreed for him in that blow, and he died. Musa said: ﴿This is of the work of Satan. Indeed, he is a manifest, misleading enemy.﴾ ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me." So He forgave him. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.﴾ ﴿He said, "My Lord, for that which You have bestowed upon me, I will never be a supporter of the criminals."﴾ i.e., by what You have granted me of rank, honor, and protection; ﴿I will never be a supporter﴾ i.e., a helper ﴿of the criminals﴾ i.e., the disbelievers in You, those who oppose Your command.

Allah the Exalted says, informing about Musa, peace be upon him [[In T: "may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him."]], when he had killed that Copt: that he woke up ﴿in the city, fearful﴾, i.e., fearing the consequences of what he had done, ﴿watching out﴾, i.e., looking about and expecting what would come of this matter. So he passed through some of the streets, and there was that man who had sought his help the day before against that Copt, fighting another man. When Musa passed by, the Israelite called on him for help against the other. Musa said to him: ﴿Indeed, you are clearly a deviator﴾, i.e., manifestly misguided and abounding in evil. Then he resolved to seize the Copt. The Israelite, because of his cowardice, weakness and humiliation, believed that Musa intended to attack him when he heard him say that. So he said, defending himself: ﴿O Musa, do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday?﴾ That was because no one knew of the killing except him and Musa, peace be upon him. When that Copt heard it, he snatched it up from his mouth [[In H and T: "he snatched it from his mouth"; the text adopted is from F and A.]] and carried it to the gate of Pharaoh and threw it down there. Thus Pharaoh learned of it, his rage intensified, and he resolved to kill Musa. So they searched for him and sent after him to bring him in for that purpose.

Thus Pharaoh learned of it, his rage intensified, and he resolved to kill Musa. So they searched for him and sent after him to bring him in for that purpose.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And there came a man﴾. He described him as a man (rajul) because he deviated from the (main) road: he took a shorter path than the path of those who had been sent after him, so he reached Musa first, and said to him: "O Musa, ﴿the chiefs are conferring about you﴾, that is, deliberating concerning you, ﴿to kill you, so leave﴾, that is, the city, ﴿indeed I am to you one of the sincere advisors﴾.

When the man told him what Pharaoh and his chiefs had conspired against him, he left Egypt alone, and his heart was not accustomed to this; rather, he had been in comfort, luxury and leadership. ﴿So he left it, fearful, looking about him vigilantly.﴾ That is, glancing about. ﴿He said, "My Lord, deliver me from the wrongdoing people."﴾ That is, from Pharaoh and his chiefs. They mention that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, sent to him an angel on a horse, who guided him to the way, and Allah knows best.

﴿And when he turned toward Madyan﴾ That is, he took a road that was clear and well-travelled, and he rejoiced at that. ﴿He said, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way."﴾ That is, to the most upright path. Allah did this for him, and guided him to the straight path in this world and the Hereafter, so he was made a guide and one who is guided.

﴿And when he arrived at the water of Madyan﴾ That is, when he reached Madyan and came to its water. It had a well which shepherds would bring their flocks to drink from. ﴿He found on it a community of people﴾ That is, a group ﴿watering [their flocks], and he found, apart from them, two women holding back﴾ That is, keeping their sheep from going to water along with the flocks of those shepherds, lest they be harmed. When Moses, peace be upon him, saw them, he felt compassion for them and had mercy on them. ﴿He said, "What is your situation?"﴾ That is, what is your news, that you do not go to water with these? ﴿They said, "We cannot water [our flocks] until the shepherds have finished [and taken their animals away]"﴾ That is, we cannot water them except after these have finished, ﴿and our father is a very old man.﴾ That is, this condition has compelled us to what you see.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So he watered [their flocks] for them.﴾ Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: Abdullah related to us, Israel informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that when Moses, peace be upon him, came to the water of Madyan, he found on it a community of people watering. He said: When they finished, they replaced the rock over the well, which no more than ten men could lift. Then he found two women holding back [their flocks]. He said: "What is your situation?" They told him, so he went to the rock and lifted it, then he drew only one bucket until the flock was satisfied. Its chain is sound. [Al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shaybah (11/530).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then he withdrew to the shade and said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need."﴾ Ibn Abbas said: Moses traveled from Egypt to Madyan with no food except herbs and tree leaves, and he was barefoot, so that by the time he reached Madyan his sandal of his foot had worn through. He sat in the shade, and he was the chosen one of Allah among His creation, and his belly was pressed against his back from hunger, and the green of the herbs could be seen through the inside of his stomach, and he was in need of even half a date.
