When Moses, peace be upon him, saw them, he felt compassion for them and had mercy on them. ﴿He said, "What is your situation?"﴾ That is, what is your news, that you do not go to water with these? ﴿They said, "We cannot water [our flocks] until the shepherds have finished [and taken their animals away]"﴾ That is, we cannot water them except after these have finished, ﴿and our father is a very old man.﴾ That is, this condition has compelled us to what you see.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So he watered [their flocks] for them.﴾ Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: Abdullah related to us, Israel informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that when Moses, peace be upon him, came to the water of Madyan, he found on it a community of people watering. He said: When they finished, they replaced the rock over the well, which no more than ten men could lift. Then he found two women holding back [their flocks]. He said: "What is your situation?" They told him, so he went to the rock and lifted it, then he drew only one bucket until the flock was satisfied. Its chain is sound. [Al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shaybah (11/530).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then he withdrew to the shade and said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need."﴾ Ibn Abbas said: Moses traveled from Egypt to Madyan with no food except herbs and tree leaves, and he was barefoot, so that by the time he reached Madyan his sandal of his foot had worn through. He sat in the shade, and he was the chosen one of Allah among His creation, and his belly was pressed against his back from hunger, and the green of the herbs could be seen through the inside of his stomach, and he was in need of even half a date.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿to the shade﴾, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud and as-Suddi said: he sat beneath a tree.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Husayn ibn Amr al-Anqazi related to me, my father related to us, Israil related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun, from Abdullah, that is Ibn Masud, who said: I hastened on a camel for two nights until I arrived at Madyan in the morning. I asked about the tree under which Moses had sheltered, and there was a green tree, flourishing. My camel lunged toward it, being hungry, and my camel took it and chewed it for a while, then spat it out. So I prayed to Allah for Moses, peace be upon him, and then I turned back. [Tafsir al-Tabari (20/37).]

It is also reported from Ibn Masud that he went to the tree from which Allah spoke to Moses, as will come, and Allah knows best.

As-Suddi said: it was of the samur tree.

Ata ibn as-Sa'ib said: When Moses said, ﴿My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need,﴾ the woman heard it.

When the man told him what Pharaoh and his chiefs had conspired against him, he left Egypt alone, and his heart was not accustomed to this; rather, he had been in comfort, luxury and leadership. ﴿So he left it, fearful, looking about him vigilantly.﴾ That is, glancing about. ﴿He said, "My Lord, deliver me from the wrongdoing people."﴾ That is, from Pharaoh and his chiefs. They mention that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, sent to him an angel on a horse, who guided him to the way, and Allah knows best.

﴿And when he turned toward Madyan﴾ That is, he took a road that was clear and well-travelled, and he rejoiced at that. ﴿He said, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way."﴾ That is, to the most upright path. Allah did this for him, and guided him to the straight path in this world and the Hereafter, so he was made a guide and one who is guided.

﴿And when he arrived at the water of Madyan﴾ That is, when he reached Madyan and came to its water. It had a well which shepherds would bring their flocks to drink from. ﴿He found on it a community of people﴾ That is, a group ﴿watering [their flocks], and he found, apart from them, two women holding back﴾ That is, keeping their sheep from going to water along with the flocks of those shepherds, lest they be harmed. When Moses, peace be upon him, saw them, he felt compassion for them and had mercy on them. ﴿He said, "What is your situation?"﴾ That is, what is your news, that you do not go to water with these? ﴿They said, "We cannot water [our flocks] until the shepherds have finished [and taken their animals away]"﴾ That is, we cannot water them except after these have finished, ﴿and our father is a very old man.﴾ That is, this condition has compelled us to what you see.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So he watered [their flocks] for them.﴾ Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: Abdullah related to us, Israel informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that when Moses, peace be upon him, came to the water of Madyan, he found on it a community of people watering. He said: When they finished, they replaced the rock over the well, which no more than ten men could lift. Then he found two women holding back [their flocks]. He said: "What is your situation?" They told him, so he went to the rock and lifted it, then he drew only one bucket until the flock was satisfied. Its chain is sound. [Al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shaybah (11/530).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then he withdrew to the shade and said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need."﴾ Ibn Abbas said: Moses traveled from Egypt to Madyan with no food except herbs and tree leaves, and he was barefoot, so that by the time he reached Madyan his sandal of his foot had worn through. He sat in the shade, and he was the chosen one of Allah among His creation, and his belly was pressed against his back from hunger, and the green of the herbs could be seen through the inside of his stomach, and he was in need of even half a date.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿to the shade﴾, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud and as-Suddi said: he sat beneath a tree.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Husayn ibn Amr al-Anqazi related to me, my father related to us, Israil related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun, from Abdullah, that is Ibn Masud, who said: I hastened on a camel for two nights until I arrived at Madyan in the morning. I asked about the tree under which Moses had sheltered, and there was a green tree, flourishing. My camel lunged toward it, being hungry, and my camel took it and chewed it for a while, then spat it out. So I prayed to Allah for Moses, peace be upon him, and then I turned back. [Tafsir al-Tabari (20/37).]

It is also reported from Ibn Masud that he went to the tree from which Allah spoke to Moses, as will come, and Allah knows best.

As-Suddi said: it was of the samur tree.

Ata ibn as-Sa'ib said: When Moses said, ﴿My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need,﴾ the woman heard it.

When the two women returned quickly with the sheep to their father, he noticed their unusual state and their quick return, so he asked them about their news. They told him what Musa (peace be upon him) had done. So he sent one of them to summon him to their father. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then one of them came to him walking shyly﴾, meaning walking like free women, as was narrated from the Commander of the Faithful, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: she was concealed by the sleeve of her garment.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Narrated to us [my father, narrated to us] Abu Nu'aym, narrated to us Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Umar ibn Maymun, who said: Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: She came walking shyly, drawing her garment over her face, not brazen (safla') nor forward and loud-voiced (kharraja wa lajja). This is a sound chain (isnad).

Al-Jawhari said: As-salfa' among men means bold; among women, the forward and bold-tongued woman; among she-camels, the strong one.

﴿She said: Indeed my father invites you so that he may reward you with the wage for what you watered for us.﴾ This is an example of courtesy in speech. She did not request him in an absolute manner, lest it suggest doubt, but said: ﴿Indeed my father invites you so that he may reward you with the wage for what you watered for us﴾, meaning: so that he may recompense you and repay you for watering our sheep. ﴿So when he came to him and related the narrative﴾, meaning: he told him what had happened to him and the cause for which he had left his land. ﴿He said: Fear not; you have escaped from the wrongdoing people.﴾ He means: be at ease and let your eye be comforted, for you have left their kingdom, so they have no authority in our lands. For this reason he said: ﴿You have escaped from the wrongdoing people.﴾

The exegetes differed about who this man was, with several opinions. One is that he was Shu'ayb the Prophet (peace be upon him), who was sent to the people of Madyan. This is the well-known view of many, and it was said by al-Hasan al-Basri and others. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Narrated to us my father, narrated to us Abd al-Aziz al-Uwaysi, narrated to us Malik ibn Anas: that it reached him that Shu'ayb is the one to whom Musa related the narrative, and he said: ﴿Fear not; you have escaped from the wrongdoing people.﴾

al-Tabarani narrated from Salama ibn Sa'd al-Anazi that he came as a delegation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said to him: "Welcome to the people of Shu'ayb and the sisters of Musa; you have been guided."

Others said: rather he was the nephew of Shu'ayb. It was also said: he was a believing man from the people of Shu'ayb. And others said: Shu'ayb lived a long time before the time of Musa (peace be upon him), because he said to his people: ﴿And the people of Lut are not far from you﴾ [Hud: 89]. The destruction of the people of Lut occurred in the time of the Friend (al-Khalil, Ibrahim) (peace be upon him), by the text of the Qur'an, and it is known that between Musa and al-Khalil, peace be upon them both, there was a long period exceeding four hundred years, as mentioned by more than one scholar. As for what was said, that Shu'ayb lived a long time, that is—and Allah knows best—a way of avoiding this difficulty. Then, among the indications that he is not Shu'ayb is that, had he been him, the Qur'an would likely have explicitly named him here. What has come in some hadiths explicitly mentioning him in the story of Musa has no sound chain, as we will mention shortly, Allah willing. Then, among what is found in the books of the Children of Israel, this man's name is "Tharun" (Thibrun), and Allah knows best.

Abu Ubayda ibn Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: Athrun, and he is the nephew of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him).

And from Abu Hamza, from Ibn Abbas: The one who hired Musa was Yathra, the lord of Madyan. Ibn Jarir narrated it, then said: The correct view is that this cannot be known except by a report, and there is no report by which proof is established regarding this.

* *

His saying: ﴿One of the two said: O my father, hire him; indeed the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.﴾ That is, one of the two daughters of this man said it. It was said: she is the one who went after Musa, peace be upon him, and she said to her father: ﴿O my father, hire him﴾, meaning: to tend this flock.

Umar, Ibn Abbas, Shurayh al-Qadi, Abu Malik, Qatada, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, and others said: When she said: ﴿Indeed the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy﴾, her father said to her: "And how do you know that?" She said: "He lifted the stone which no more than ten men could lift, and when I came with him, I walked ahead of him; he said to me: 'Be behind me, and if I deviate from the path, throw a pebble so I may know the way, that I may be guided by it.'"

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Ubayda, from Abdullah, that is Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The most perceptive of people are three: Abu Bakr, when he perceived in Umar; the companion of Yusuf, when he said: ﴿Make his residence honorable﴾ [Yusuf: 21]; and the companion of Musa, when she said: ﴿O my father, hire him; indeed the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.﴾

He said: ﴿Indeed I intend to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine﴾, meaning: this elderly old man asked him to tend his sheep and to marry him to one of his two daughters.

Shu'ayb al-Jibba'i said: They are Safura and Layya.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Safura and Shar'a, and it is said Layya. The followers of Abu Hanifa (may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him) have used this verse as evidence for the validity of a sale in a case where one says: "I sell you one of these two slaves for a hundred," and the other says: "I have bought," that it is valid, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿On condition that you serve me for eight years, and if you complete ten, it is from you.﴾ That is, on condition that you tend for me eight years; if you voluntarily add two years, then it is up to you, and otherwise eight years suffice. ﴿And I do not intend to burden you; you will find me, Allah willing, among the righteous.﴾ That is, I will not impose hardship on you, nor harass you, nor dispute with you.

They have used this noble verse as evidence for the view of al-Awza'i, in the case where one says: "I sell you this for ten in cash, or for twenty on credit," that it is valid, and the buyer chooses whichever of the two he takes, and it is valid. The hadith narrated in Sunan Abi Dawud: "Whoever makes two sales in one sale, then he has the lesser of the two or usury" has been interpreted in accordance with this view. Regarding the use of this verse and this hadith as evidence for this view, there is room for examination, but this is not the place to expand upon it because of its length, and Allah knows best.

Then the companions of Imam Ahmad and those who followed them have used this verse as evidence for the validity of hiring a worker for food and clothing, and they took comfort in what Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Majah narrated in his book, the Sunan, where he said: "Chapter: Hiring a worker for the food of his belly." Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa al-Himsi narrated to us, Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Maslama ibn Ali, from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, from al-Harith ibn Yazid, from Ali ibn Rabah, who said: I heard Utba ibn al-Nadr say: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he recited Ta-Sin-Mim, until he reached the story of Musa, and he said: 'Indeed Musa hired himself out for eight years, or ten years, in exchange for the chastity of his private parts and the food of his belly.'"

This hadith through this chain is weak, because Maslama ibn Ali, who is al-Khushani al-Dimashqi al-Balati, is weak in narration according to the imams. But it has been narrated through another chain, and there is also room for examination in it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Narrated to us Abu Zur'a, narrated to us Safwan, narrated to us al-Walid, narrated to us Abdullah ibn Lahi'a, from al-Harith ibn Yazid al-Hadrami, from Ali ibn Rabah al-Lakhmi, who said: I heard Utba ibn al-Nadr al-Sulami, companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), narrate that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Musa hired himself out for the chastity of his private parts and the food of his belly."

* *

His saying, the Exalted, reporting about Musa (peace be upon him): ﴿He said: That is between me and you; whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there shall be no injustice against me; and Allah is Witness over what we say.﴾ He means: Musa said to his father-in-law: The matter is as you have said, that you hired me for eight years, and if I complete ten, it is from me. So whenever I do the lesser of the two, I am free from the covenant and out of the condition. For this reason he said: ﴿Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there shall be no injustice against me﴾, meaning: there is no blame upon me. Although the complete option is permissible, it is superior for another reason, by external evidence, just as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 203].

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Hamza ibn Amr al-Aslami (may Allah be pleased with him), who fasted often, when he asked him about fasting while traveling: "If you wish, fast, and if you wish, break your fast" [narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (3/493) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan (4/185)], although fasting is preferable by other evidence.

Now, the evidence indicates that Musa (peace be upon him) only did the more complete and perfect of the two terms. Al-Bukhari said:

Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Marwan ibn Shuja' narrated to us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A Jew from the people of al-Hira asked me: "Which of the two terms did Musa fulfill?" I said: "I do not know, until I go to the scholar of the Arabs and ask him." So I went and asked Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him), and he said: "He fulfilled the more and the better of them both, for indeed when the Messenger of Allah said something, he did it." This is how al-Bukhari narrated it [Sahih al-Bukhari (2684)], and this is how Hakim ibn Jubayr and others narrated it from Sa'id ibn Jubayr. In the "Hadith of the Trials" narrated by al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, it occurs that the one who asked him was a man from the Christians. The first is more correct, and Allah knows best. It has also been narrated through mursal chains from a hadith of Ibn Abbas raised to the Prophet (ﷺ). Ibn Jarir said:

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi narrated to us, al-Humaydi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Abi Ya'qub narrated to me, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked Jibril: 'Which of the two terms did Musa fulfill?' He said: 'The more complete and the more perfect of them.'" [Tafsir al-Tabari (20/44)].

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, from his father, from al-Humaydi, from Sufyan, that is Ibn Uyayna, who said: Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Abi Ya'qub narrated to me, and he was one of my elders or younger than me, and he mentioned it.

I say: This Ibrahim is not well known.

The Hadith narrated by al-Bazzar from Ahmad ibn Abān al-Qurashī, from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, from Ibrāhīm ibn Aʿyan, from al-Ḥakam ibn Abān, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with the same wording as above. He then said: "We do not know it to be attributed to the Prophet (ﷺ) through Ibn ʿAbbās except through this route."[[Al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar said in Lisān al-Mīzān (1/124): "Ibrāhīm ibn Yaḥyā al-ʿAdanī, from al-Ḥakam ibn Abān, and from him Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, with a munkar report, and the man is unknown (nakirah). His narration from al-Ḥumaydī, and its text: The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked, and Jibrīl (peace be upon him) [was asked] which of the two terms Mūsā fulfilled." End of quote. Ibn Ḥibbān mentioned this man in al-Thiqāt. Al-Azdī said: 'His narration is not followed.' Al-Ḥākim recorded his aforementioned Hadith in al-Mustadrak.]]

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: It was read to Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā; Ibn Wahb informed us; ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed us; from Yaḥyā ibn Maymūn al-Ḥaḍramī, from Yūsuf ibn Tayraḥ: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "I have no knowledge." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked Jibrīl, and Jibrīl said: "I have no knowledge." Then Jibrīl asked an angel above him, and he said: "I have no knowledge." Then that angel asked his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, about what Jibrīl had asked him, which Muḥammad (ﷺ) had asked. The Lord, glorified and exalted, said: "He fulfilled the more righteous and the more lasting of them both, or he said: the purer of them both."[[Musnad al-Bazzār, no. 2245 (Kashf al-Astār).]]

This is mursal (a report in which the Successor omits the Companion from the chain), and it has come in a mursal form through another route. Sunayd said: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujāhid said: The Prophet (ﷺ) asked Jibrīl: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "I will ask Isrāfīl." So he asked him, and he said: "I will ask the Lord, Mighty and Majestic." So he asked Him, and He said: "He fulfilled the more righteous and the more complete of them both."[[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (20/44).]]

Another mursal route: Ibn Jarīr said: Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Abū Maʿshar narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazī, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "The more complete and the more perfect of them both."[[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (20/44).]]

These routes reinforce one another (mutaʿāḍidah). Moreover, it has been narrated as a marfūʿ (attributed to the Prophet) report from the narration of Abū Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Ḥāfiẓ Abū Bakr al-Bazzār said: Abū ʿUbaydillāh Yaḥyā ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Sakan narrated to us; Isḥāq ibn Idrīs narrated to us; ʿAwbad ibn Abī ʿImrān al-Jawnī narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ṣāmit, from Abū Dharr: that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "The more complete of them both and the more righteous of them both." He said: "And if you are asked which of the two women he married, then say: the younger of them."

Then al-Bazzār said: "We do not know of anything narrated from Abū Dharr except through this chain."[[Musnad al-Bazzār, no. 2244 (Kashf al-Astār).]]

Ibn Abī Ḥātim also narrated it from the Ḥadīth of ʿAwbad ibn Abī ʿImrān, who is ḍaʿīf (weak). Similar wording has also been narrated from the Ḥadīth of ʿUtbah ibn al-Nuddar [in some copies: al-Mundhir], with an extremely strange addition. Abū Bakr al-Bazzār said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb al-Sijistānī narrated to us; Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr narrated to us; Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us; al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Rabāḥ al-Lakhmī, who said: I heard ʿUtbah ibn al-Nuddar [in some copies: al-Mundhir] say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "The more righteous of them both and the more complete of them both." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When Mūsā, peace be upon him, wanted to part from Shuʿayb, peace be upon him, he instructed his wife to ask her father to give her some of his sheep on which they could live. So he gave her whatever his sheep bore that year of various colours. He said: Every ewe that passed, Mūsā struck its side with his staff, and they bore spotted offspring of all colours, and each ewe bore twins and triplets, none of them being fashūsh, nor ḍabūb, nor kamīshah that escapes the palm, nor thaʿūl." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you conquer al-Shām, you will indeed find remnants of them, and they are the Sāmiriyyah."[[Musnad al-Bazzār, no. 2246 (Kashf al-Astār).]]

This is how al-Bazzār reported it. Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated it in a fuller form than this, saying:

Abū Zurʿah narrated to us; Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Bukayr narrated to me; ʿAbdullāh ibn Lahīʿah narrated to me (ḥ). And Abū Zurʿah narrated to us; Ṣafwān narrated to us; al-Walīd narrated to us; ʿAbdullāh ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd al-Ḥaḍramī, from ʿAlī ibn Rabāḥ al-Lakhmī, who said: I heard ʿUtbah ibn al-Nudḍar [in some copies: al-Mundhir] al-Sulamī, the Companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), narrating that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Mūsā, peace be upon him, hired himself out in exchange for the chastity of his private part and the sustenance of his belly. When the term was fulfilled, it was said: O Messenger of Allah, which of the two terms? He said: The more righteous of them both and the more complete of them both. When he wanted to part from Shuʿayb, he instructed his wife to ask her father to give her some of his sheep on which they could live. So he gave her what his sheep bore of the colours of those born that year. His sheep were black and beautiful. Mūsā, peace be upon him, went to his staff, peeled it from its tip, then placed it at the lowest part of the trough, then brought the sheep and gave them drink, and Mūsā stood facing the trough. No ewe came out of it without him striking its side, ewe by ewe. He said: So they came into heat and conceived twice and thrice, and all of them bore various-coloured offspring, except one or two ewes, in which there was no fashūsh." Al-Walīd said: "Ḍabūn," and Ṣafwān said: "Ḍabūb." Abū Zurʿah said: "The correct form is ḍabūb, and neither ʿazūz, nor thaʿūl, nor kamīshah that escapes the palm." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "So if you conquer al-Shām, you will find remnants of those sheep, and they are the Sāmiriyyah."

And Abū Zurʿah narrated to us; Ṣafwān narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Walīd say: I asked Ibn Lahīʿah: What is the fashūsh? He said: The one that spills its milk, with a wide teat-opening. I said: What is the ḍabūb? He said: The one with a long udder that drags. I said: What is the ʿazūz? He said: The one with a narrow teat-opening. He said: What is the thaʿūl? He said: The one that has no udder except like two nipples. I said: What is the kamīshah? He said: The one that escapes the palm, having a small udder that the hand cannot grasp.

The core of this Ḥadīth rests on ʿAbdullāh ibn Lahīʿah al-Miṣrī, in whose memory there is weakness, and I fear that raising it to the Prophet (ﷺ) was an error, and Allah knows best. It should be narrated as "there is no fashūsh, no ʿazūz, no ḍabūb, no thaʿūl, and no kamīshah," so that each deficient attribute is mentioned together with its corresponding deficient attributes. Ibn Jarīr also narrated from the words of Anas ibn Mālik, as a statement attributed to him (mawqūf), something that approximates parts of this with a good chain. He said: Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us; Muʿādh ibn Hishām narrated to us; my father narrated to us, from Qatādah, who said: Anas ibn Mālik, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us: When the Prophet of Allah, Mūsā, peace be upon him, called his companion to the term that was between them, his companion said to him: "Every ewe that gives birth to a colour other than its own, that offspring is yours." So he went and set up poles over the water. When the ewes saw the shapes, they were frightened and wheeled around, and all of them gave birth to piebald (bulq) offspring, except one ewe. So he took their offspring away that year.[[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (20/44).]]

When the two women returned quickly with the sheep to their father, he noticed their unusual state and their quick return, so he asked them about their news. They told him what Musa (peace be upon him) had done. So he sent one of them to summon him to their father. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then one of them came to him walking shyly﴾, meaning walking like free women, as was narrated from the Commander of the Faithful, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: she was concealed by the sleeve of her garment.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Narrated to us [my father, narrated to us] Abu Nu'aym, narrated to us Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Umar ibn Maymun, who said: Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: She came walking shyly, drawing her garment over her face, not brazen (safla') nor forward and loud-voiced (kharraja wa lajja). This is a sound chain (isnad).

Al-Jawhari said: As-salfa' among men means bold; among women, the forward and bold-tongued woman; among she-camels, the strong one.

﴿She said: Indeed my father invites you so that he may reward you with the wage for what you watered for us.﴾ This is an example of courtesy in speech. She did not request him in an absolute manner, lest it suggest doubt, but said: ﴿Indeed my father invites you so that he may reward you with the wage for what you watered for us﴾, meaning: so that he may recompense you and repay you for watering our sheep. ﴿So when he came to him and related the narrative﴾, meaning: he told him what had happened to him and the cause for which he had left his land. ﴿He said: Fear not; you have escaped from the wrongdoing people.﴾ He means: be at ease and let your eye be comforted, for you have left their kingdom, so they have no authority in our lands. For this reason he said: ﴿You have escaped from the wrongdoing people.﴾

The exegetes differed about who this man was, with several opinions. One is that he was Shu'ayb the Prophet (peace be upon him), who was sent to the people of Madyan. This is the well-known view of many, and it was said by al-Hasan al-Basri and others. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Narrated to us my father, narrated to us Abd al-Aziz al-Uwaysi, narrated to us Malik ibn Anas: that it reached him that Shu'ayb is the one to whom Musa related the narrative, and he said: ﴿Fear not; you have escaped from the wrongdoing people.﴾

al-Tabarani narrated from Salama ibn Sa'd al-Anazi that he came as a delegation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said to him: "Welcome to the people of Shu'ayb and the sisters of Musa; you have been guided."

Others said: rather he was the nephew of Shu'ayb. It was also said: he was a believing man from the people of Shu'ayb. And others said: Shu'ayb lived a long time before the time of Musa (peace be upon him), because he said to his people: ﴿And the people of Lut are not far from you﴾ [Hud: 89]. The destruction of the people of Lut occurred in the time of the Friend (al-Khalil, Ibrahim) (peace be upon him), by the text of the Qur'an, and it is known that between Musa and al-Khalil, peace be upon them both, there was a long period exceeding four hundred years, as mentioned by more than one scholar. As for what was said, that Shu'ayb lived a long time, that is—and Allah knows best—a way of avoiding this difficulty. Then, among the indications that he is not Shu'ayb is that, had he been him, the Qur'an would likely have explicitly named him here. What has come in some hadiths explicitly mentioning him in the story of Musa has no sound chain, as we will mention shortly, Allah willing. Then, among what is found in the books of the Children of Israel, this man's name is "Tharun" (Thibrun), and Allah knows best.

Abu Ubayda ibn Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: Athrun, and he is the nephew of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him).

And from Abu Hamza, from Ibn Abbas: The one who hired Musa was Yathra, the lord of Madyan. Ibn Jarir narrated it, then said: The correct view is that this cannot be known except by a report, and there is no report by which proof is established regarding this.

* *

His saying: ﴿One of the two said: O my father, hire him; indeed the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.﴾ That is, one of the two daughters of this man said it. It was said: she is the one who went after Musa, peace be upon him, and she said to her father: ﴿O my father, hire him﴾, meaning: to tend this flock.

Umar, Ibn Abbas, Shurayh al-Qadi, Abu Malik, Qatada, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, and others said: When she said: ﴿Indeed the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy﴾, her father said to her: "And how do you know that?" She said: "He lifted the stone which no more than ten men could lift, and when I came with him, I walked ahead of him; he said to me: 'Be behind me, and if I deviate from the path, throw a pebble so I may know the way, that I may be guided by it.'"

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Ubayda, from Abdullah, that is Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The most perceptive of people are three: Abu Bakr, when he perceived in Umar; the companion of Yusuf, when he said: ﴿Make his residence honorable﴾ [Yusuf: 21]; and the companion of Musa, when she said: ﴿O my father, hire him; indeed the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.﴾

He said: ﴿Indeed I intend to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine﴾, meaning: this elderly old man asked him to tend his sheep and to marry him to one of his two daughters.

Shu'ayb al-Jibba'i said: They are Safura and Layya.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Safura and Shar'a, and it is said Layya. The followers of Abu Hanifa (may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him) have used this verse as evidence for the validity of a sale in a case where one says: "I sell you one of these two slaves for a hundred," and the other says: "I have bought," that it is valid, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿On condition that you serve me for eight years, and if you complete ten, it is from you.﴾ That is, on condition that you tend for me eight years; if you voluntarily add two years, then it is up to you, and otherwise eight years suffice. ﴿And I do not intend to burden you; you will find me, Allah willing, among the righteous.﴾ That is, I will not impose hardship on you, nor harass you, nor dispute with you.

They have used this noble verse as evidence for the view of al-Awza'i, in the case where one says: "I sell you this for ten in cash, or for twenty on credit," that it is valid, and the buyer chooses whichever of the two he takes, and it is valid. The hadith narrated in Sunan Abi Dawud: "Whoever makes two sales in one sale, then he has the lesser of the two or usury" has been interpreted in accordance with this view. Regarding the use of this verse and this hadith as evidence for this view, there is room for examination, but this is not the place to expand upon it because of its length, and Allah knows best.

Then the companions of Imam Ahmad and those who followed them have used this verse as evidence for the validity of hiring a worker for food and clothing, and they took comfort in what Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Majah narrated in his book, the Sunan, where he said: "Chapter: Hiring a worker for the food of his belly." Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa al-Himsi narrated to us, Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Maslama ibn Ali, from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, from al-Harith ibn Yazid, from Ali ibn Rabah, who said: I heard Utba ibn al-Nadr say: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he recited Ta-Sin-Mim, until he reached the story of Musa, and he said: 'Indeed Musa hired himself out for eight years, or ten years, in exchange for the chastity of his private parts and the food of his belly.'"

This hadith through this chain is weak, because Maslama ibn Ali, who is al-Khushani al-Dimashqi al-Balati, is weak in narration according to the imams. But it has been narrated through another chain, and there is also room for examination in it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Narrated to us Abu Zur'a, narrated to us Safwan, narrated to us al-Walid, narrated to us Abdullah ibn Lahi'a, from al-Harith ibn Yazid al-Hadrami, from Ali ibn Rabah al-Lakhmi, who said: I heard Utba ibn al-Nadr al-Sulami, companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), narrate that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Musa hired himself out for the chastity of his private parts and the food of his belly."

* *

His saying, the Exalted, reporting about Musa (peace be upon him): ﴿He said: That is between me and you; whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there shall be no injustice against me; and Allah is Witness over what we say.﴾ He means: Musa said to his father-in-law: The matter is as you have said, that you hired me for eight years, and if I complete ten, it is from me. So whenever I do the lesser of the two, I am free from the covenant and out of the condition. For this reason he said: ﴿Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there shall be no injustice against me﴾, meaning: there is no blame upon me. Although the complete option is permissible, it is superior for another reason, by external evidence, just as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 203].

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Hamza ibn Amr al-Aslami (may Allah be pleased with him), who fasted often, when he asked him about fasting while traveling: "If you wish, fast, and if you wish, break your fast" [narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (3/493) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan (4/185)], although fasting is preferable by other evidence.

Now, the evidence indicates that Musa (peace be upon him) only did the more complete and perfect of the two terms. Al-Bukhari said:

Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Marwan ibn Shuja' narrated to us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A Jew from the people of al-Hira asked me: "Which of the two terms did Musa fulfill?" I said: "I do not know, until I go to the scholar of the Arabs and ask him." So I went and asked Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him), and he said: "He fulfilled the more and the better of them both, for indeed when the Messenger of Allah said something, he did it." This is how al-Bukhari narrated it [Sahih al-Bukhari (2684)], and this is how Hakim ibn Jubayr and others narrated it from Sa'id ibn Jubayr. In the "Hadith of the Trials" narrated by al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, it occurs that the one who asked him was a man from the Christians. The first is more correct, and Allah knows best. It has also been narrated through mursal chains from a hadith of Ibn Abbas raised to the Prophet (ﷺ). Ibn Jarir said:

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi narrated to us, al-Humaydi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Abi Ya'qub narrated to me, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked Jibril: 'Which of the two terms did Musa fulfill?' He said: 'The more complete and the more perfect of them.'" [Tafsir al-Tabari (20/44)].

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, from his father, from al-Humaydi, from Sufyan, that is Ibn Uyayna, who said: Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Abi Ya'qub narrated to me, and he was one of my elders or younger than me, and he mentioned it.

I say: This Ibrahim is not well known.

The Hadith narrated by al-Bazzar from Ahmad ibn Abān al-Qurashī, from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, from Ibrāhīm ibn Aʿyan, from al-Ḥakam ibn Abān, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with the same wording as above. He then said: "We do not know it to be attributed to the Prophet (ﷺ) through Ibn ʿAbbās except through this route."[[Al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar said in Lisān al-Mīzān (1/124): "Ibrāhīm ibn Yaḥyā al-ʿAdanī, from al-Ḥakam ibn Abān, and from him Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, with a munkar report, and the man is unknown (nakirah). His narration from al-Ḥumaydī, and its text: The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked, and Jibrīl (peace be upon him) [was asked] which of the two terms Mūsā fulfilled." End of quote. Ibn Ḥibbān mentioned this man in al-Thiqāt. Al-Azdī said: 'His narration is not followed.' Al-Ḥākim recorded his aforementioned Hadith in al-Mustadrak.]]

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: It was read to Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā; Ibn Wahb informed us; ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed us; from Yaḥyā ibn Maymūn al-Ḥaḍramī, from Yūsuf ibn Tayraḥ: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "I have no knowledge." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked Jibrīl, and Jibrīl said: "I have no knowledge." Then Jibrīl asked an angel above him, and he said: "I have no knowledge." Then that angel asked his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, about what Jibrīl had asked him, which Muḥammad (ﷺ) had asked. The Lord, glorified and exalted, said: "He fulfilled the more righteous and the more lasting of them both, or he said: the purer of them both."[[Musnad al-Bazzār, no. 2245 (Kashf al-Astār).]]

This is mursal (a report in which the Successor omits the Companion from the chain), and it has come in a mursal form through another route. Sunayd said: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujāhid said: The Prophet (ﷺ) asked Jibrīl: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "I will ask Isrāfīl." So he asked him, and he said: "I will ask the Lord, Mighty and Majestic." So he asked Him, and He said: "He fulfilled the more righteous and the more complete of them both."[[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (20/44).]]

Another mursal route: Ibn Jarīr said: Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Abū Maʿshar narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazī, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "The more complete and the more perfect of them both."[[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (20/44).]]

These routes reinforce one another (mutaʿāḍidah). Moreover, it has been narrated as a marfūʿ (attributed to the Prophet) report from the narration of Abū Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Ḥāfiẓ Abū Bakr al-Bazzār said: Abū ʿUbaydillāh Yaḥyā ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Sakan narrated to us; Isḥāq ibn Idrīs narrated to us; ʿAwbad ibn Abī ʿImrān al-Jawnī narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ṣāmit, from Abū Dharr: that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "The more complete of them both and the more righteous of them both." He said: "And if you are asked which of the two women he married, then say: the younger of them."

Then al-Bazzār said: "We do not know of anything narrated from Abū Dharr except through this chain."[[Musnad al-Bazzār, no. 2244 (Kashf al-Astār).]]

Ibn Abī Ḥātim also narrated it from the Ḥadīth of ʿAwbad ibn Abī ʿImrān, who is ḍaʿīf (weak). Similar wording has also been narrated from the Ḥadīth of ʿUtbah ibn al-Nuddar [in some copies: al-Mundhir], with an extremely strange addition. Abū Bakr al-Bazzār said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb al-Sijistānī narrated to us; Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr narrated to us; Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us; al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Rabāḥ al-Lakhmī, who said: I heard ʿUtbah ibn al-Nuddar [in some copies: al-Mundhir] say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "The more righteous of them both and the more complete of them both." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When Mūsā, peace be upon him, wanted to part from Shuʿayb, peace be upon him, he instructed his wife to ask her father to give her some of his sheep on which they could live. So he gave her whatever his sheep bore that year of various colours. He said: Every ewe that passed, Mūsā struck its side with his staff, and they bore spotted offspring of all colours, and each ewe bore twins and triplets, none of them being fashūsh, nor ḍabūb, nor kamīshah that escapes the palm, nor thaʿūl." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you conquer al-Shām, you will indeed find remnants of them, and they are the Sāmiriyyah."[[Musnad al-Bazzār, no. 2246 (Kashf al-Astār).]]

This is how al-Bazzār reported it. Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated it in a fuller form than this, saying:

Abū Zurʿah narrated to us; Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Bukayr narrated to me; ʿAbdullāh ibn Lahīʿah narrated to me (ḥ). And Abū Zurʿah narrated to us; Ṣafwān narrated to us; al-Walīd narrated to us; ʿAbdullāh ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd al-Ḥaḍramī, from ʿAlī ibn Rabāḥ al-Lakhmī, who said: I heard ʿUtbah ibn al-Nudḍar [in some copies: al-Mundhir] al-Sulamī, the Companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), narrating that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Mūsā, peace be upon him, hired himself out in exchange for the chastity of his private part and the sustenance of his belly. When the term was fulfilled, it was said: O Messenger of Allah, which of the two terms? He said: The more righteous of them both and the more complete of them both. When he wanted to part from Shuʿayb, he instructed his wife to ask her father to give her some of his sheep on which they could live. So he gave her what his sheep bore of the colours of those born that year. His sheep were black and beautiful. Mūsā, peace be upon him, went to his staff, peeled it from its tip, then placed it at the lowest part of the trough, then brought the sheep and gave them drink, and Mūsā stood facing the trough. No ewe came out of it without him striking its side, ewe by ewe. He said: So they came into heat and conceived twice and thrice, and all of them bore various-coloured offspring, except one or two ewes, in which there was no fashūsh." Al-Walīd said: "Ḍabūn," and Ṣafwān said: "Ḍabūb." Abū Zurʿah said: "The correct form is ḍabūb, and neither ʿazūz, nor thaʿūl, nor kamīshah that escapes the palm." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "So if you conquer al-Shām, you will find remnants of those sheep, and they are the Sāmiriyyah."

And Abū Zurʿah narrated to us; Ṣafwān narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Walīd say: I asked Ibn Lahīʿah: What is the fashūsh? He said: The one that spills its milk, with a wide teat-opening. I said: What is the ḍabūb? He said: The one with a long udder that drags. I said: What is the ʿazūz? He said: The one with a narrow teat-opening. He said: What is the thaʿūl? He said: The one that has no udder except like two nipples. I said: What is the kamīshah? He said: The one that escapes the palm, having a small udder that the hand cannot grasp.

The core of this Ḥadīth rests on ʿAbdullāh ibn Lahīʿah al-Miṣrī, in whose memory there is weakness, and I fear that raising it to the Prophet (ﷺ) was an error, and Allah knows best. It should be narrated as "there is no fashūsh, no ʿazūz, no ḍabūb, no thaʿūl, and no kamīshah," so that each deficient attribute is mentioned together with its corresponding deficient attributes. Ibn Jarīr also narrated from the words of Anas ibn Mālik, as a statement attributed to him (mawqūf), something that approximates parts of this with a good chain. He said: Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us; Muʿādh ibn Hishām narrated to us; my father narrated to us, from Qatādah, who said: Anas ibn Mālik, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us: When the Prophet of Allah, Mūsā, peace be upon him, called his companion to the term that was between them, his companion said to him: "Every ewe that gives birth to a colour other than its own, that offspring is yours." So he went and set up poles over the water. When the ewes saw the shapes, they were frightened and wheeled around, and all of them gave birth to piebald (bulq) offspring, except one ewe. So he took their offspring away that year.[[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (20/44).]]

When the two women returned quickly with the sheep to their father, he noticed their unusual state and their quick return, so he asked them about their news. They told him what Musa (peace be upon him) had done. So he sent one of them to summon him to their father. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then one of them came to him walking shyly﴾, meaning walking like free women, as was narrated from the Commander of the Faithful, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: she was concealed by the sleeve of her garment.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Narrated to us [my father, narrated to us] Abu Nu'aym, narrated to us Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Umar ibn Maymun, who said: Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: She came walking shyly, drawing her garment over her face, not brazen (safla') nor forward and loud-voiced (kharraja wa lajja). This is a sound chain (isnad).

Al-Jawhari said: As-salfa' among men means bold; among women, the forward and bold-tongued woman; among she-camels, the strong one.

﴿She said: Indeed my father invites you so that he may reward you with the wage for what you watered for us.﴾ This is an example of courtesy in speech. She did not request him in an absolute manner, lest it suggest doubt, but said: ﴿Indeed my father invites you so that he may reward you with the wage for what you watered for us﴾, meaning: so that he may recompense you and repay you for watering our sheep. ﴿So when he came to him and related the narrative﴾, meaning: he told him what had happened to him and the cause for which he had left his land. ﴿He said: Fear not; you have escaped from the wrongdoing people.﴾ He means: be at ease and let your eye be comforted, for you have left their kingdom, so they have no authority in our lands. For this reason he said: ﴿You have escaped from the wrongdoing people.﴾

The exegetes differed about who this man was, with several opinions. One is that he was Shu'ayb the Prophet (peace be upon him), who was sent to the people of Madyan. This is the well-known view of many, and it was said by al-Hasan al-Basri and others. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Narrated to us my father, narrated to us Abd al-Aziz al-Uwaysi, narrated to us Malik ibn Anas: that it reached him that Shu'ayb is the one to whom Musa related the narrative, and he said: ﴿Fear not; you have escaped from the wrongdoing people.﴾

al-Tabarani narrated from Salama ibn Sa'd al-Anazi that he came as a delegation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said to him: "Welcome to the people of Shu'ayb and the sisters of Musa; you have been guided."

Others said: rather he was the nephew of Shu'ayb. It was also said: he was a believing man from the people of Shu'ayb. And others said: Shu'ayb lived a long time before the time of Musa (peace be upon him), because he said to his people: ﴿And the people of Lut are not far from you﴾ [Hud: 89]. The destruction of the people of Lut occurred in the time of the Friend (al-Khalil, Ibrahim) (peace be upon him), by the text of the Qur'an, and it is known that between Musa and al-Khalil, peace be upon them both, there was a long period exceeding four hundred years, as mentioned by more than one scholar. As for what was said, that Shu'ayb lived a long time, that is—and Allah knows best—a way of avoiding this difficulty. Then, among the indications that he is not Shu'ayb is that, had he been him, the Qur'an would likely have explicitly named him here. What has come in some hadiths explicitly mentioning him in the story of Musa has no sound chain, as we will mention shortly, Allah willing. Then, among what is found in the books of the Children of Israel, this man's name is "Tharun" (Thibrun), and Allah knows best.

Abu Ubayda ibn Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: Athrun, and he is the nephew of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him).

And from Abu Hamza, from Ibn Abbas: The one who hired Musa was Yathra, the lord of Madyan. Ibn Jarir narrated it, then said: The correct view is that this cannot be known except by a report, and there is no report by which proof is established regarding this.

* *

His saying: ﴿One of the two said: O my father, hire him; indeed the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.﴾ That is, one of the two daughters of this man said it. It was said: she is the one who went after Musa, peace be upon him, and she said to her father: ﴿O my father, hire him﴾, meaning: to tend this flock.

Umar, Ibn Abbas, Shurayh al-Qadi, Abu Malik, Qatada, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, and others said: When she said: ﴿Indeed the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy﴾, her father said to her: "And how do you know that?" She said: "He lifted the stone which no more than ten men could lift, and when I came with him, I walked ahead of him; he said to me: 'Be behind me, and if I deviate from the path, throw a pebble so I may know the way, that I may be guided by it.'"

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Ubayda, from Abdullah, that is Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The most perceptive of people are three: Abu Bakr, when he perceived in Umar; the companion of Yusuf, when he said: ﴿Make his residence honorable﴾ [Yusuf: 21]; and the companion of Musa, when she said: ﴿O my father, hire him; indeed the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.﴾

He said: ﴿Indeed I intend to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine﴾, meaning: this elderly old man asked him to tend his sheep and to marry him to one of his two daughters.

Shu'ayb al-Jibba'i said: They are Safura and Layya.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Safura and Shar'a, and it is said Layya. The followers of Abu Hanifa (may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him) have used this verse as evidence for the validity of a sale in a case where one says: "I sell you one of these two slaves for a hundred," and the other says: "I have bought," that it is valid, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿On condition that you serve me for eight years, and if you complete ten, it is from you.﴾ That is, on condition that you tend for me eight years; if you voluntarily add two years, then it is up to you, and otherwise eight years suffice. ﴿And I do not intend to burden you; you will find me, Allah willing, among the righteous.﴾ That is, I will not impose hardship on you, nor harass you, nor dispute with you.

They have used this noble verse as evidence for the view of al-Awza'i, in the case where one says: "I sell you this for ten in cash, or for twenty on credit," that it is valid, and the buyer chooses whichever of the two he takes, and it is valid. The hadith narrated in Sunan Abi Dawud: "Whoever makes two sales in one sale, then he has the lesser of the two or usury" has been interpreted in accordance with this view. Regarding the use of this verse and this hadith as evidence for this view, there is room for examination, but this is not the place to expand upon it because of its length, and Allah knows best.

Then the companions of Imam Ahmad and those who followed them have used this verse as evidence for the validity of hiring a worker for food and clothing, and they took comfort in what Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Majah narrated in his book, the Sunan, where he said: "Chapter: Hiring a worker for the food of his belly." Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa al-Himsi narrated to us, Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Maslama ibn Ali, from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, from al-Harith ibn Yazid, from Ali ibn Rabah, who said: I heard Utba ibn al-Nadr say: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he recited Ta-Sin-Mim, until he reached the story of Musa, and he said: 'Indeed Musa hired himself out for eight years, or ten years, in exchange for the chastity of his private parts and the food of his belly.'"

This hadith through this chain is weak, because Maslama ibn Ali, who is al-Khushani al-Dimashqi al-Balati, is weak in narration according to the imams. But it has been narrated through another chain, and there is also room for examination in it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Narrated to us Abu Zur'a, narrated to us Safwan, narrated to us al-Walid, narrated to us Abdullah ibn Lahi'a, from al-Harith ibn Yazid al-Hadrami, from Ali ibn Rabah al-Lakhmi, who said: I heard Utba ibn al-Nadr al-Sulami, companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), narrate that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Musa hired himself out for the chastity of his private parts and the food of his belly."

* *

His saying, the Exalted, reporting about Musa (peace be upon him): ﴿He said: That is between me and you; whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there shall be no injustice against me; and Allah is Witness over what we say.﴾ He means: Musa said to his father-in-law: The matter is as you have said, that you hired me for eight years, and if I complete ten, it is from me. So whenever I do the lesser of the two, I am free from the covenant and out of the condition. For this reason he said: ﴿Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there shall be no injustice against me﴾, meaning: there is no blame upon me. Although the complete option is permissible, it is superior for another reason, by external evidence, just as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him, and whoever delays, there is no sin upon him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 203].

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Hamza ibn Amr al-Aslami (may Allah be pleased with him), who fasted often, when he asked him about fasting while traveling: "If you wish, fast, and if you wish, break your fast" [narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (3/493) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan (4/185)], although fasting is preferable by other evidence.

Now, the evidence indicates that Musa (peace be upon him) only did the more complete and perfect of the two terms. Al-Bukhari said:

Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Marwan ibn Shuja' narrated to us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A Jew from the people of al-Hira asked me: "Which of the two terms did Musa fulfill?" I said: "I do not know, until I go to the scholar of the Arabs and ask him." So I went and asked Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him), and he said: "He fulfilled the more and the better of them both, for indeed when the Messenger of Allah said something, he did it." This is how al-Bukhari narrated it [Sahih al-Bukhari (2684)], and this is how Hakim ibn Jubayr and others narrated it from Sa'id ibn Jubayr. In the "Hadith of the Trials" narrated by al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, it occurs that the one who asked him was a man from the Christians. The first is more correct, and Allah knows best. It has also been narrated through mursal chains from a hadith of Ibn Abbas raised to the Prophet (ﷺ). Ibn Jarir said:

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi narrated to us, al-Humaydi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Abi Ya'qub narrated to me, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked Jibril: 'Which of the two terms did Musa fulfill?' He said: 'The more complete and the more perfect of them.'" [Tafsir al-Tabari (20/44)].

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, from his father, from al-Humaydi, from Sufyan, that is Ibn Uyayna, who said: Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Abi Ya'qub narrated to me, and he was one of my elders or younger than me, and he mentioned it.

I say: This Ibrahim is not well known.

The Hadith narrated by al-Bazzar from Ahmad ibn Abān al-Qurashī, from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, from Ibrāhīm ibn Aʿyan, from al-Ḥakam ibn Abān, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with the same wording as above. He then said: "We do not know it to be attributed to the Prophet (ﷺ) through Ibn ʿAbbās except through this route."[[Al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar said in Lisān al-Mīzān (1/124): "Ibrāhīm ibn Yaḥyā al-ʿAdanī, from al-Ḥakam ibn Abān, and from him Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, with a munkar report, and the man is unknown (nakirah). His narration from al-Ḥumaydī, and its text: The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked, and Jibrīl (peace be upon him) [was asked] which of the two terms Mūsā fulfilled." End of quote. Ibn Ḥibbān mentioned this man in al-Thiqāt. Al-Azdī said: 'His narration is not followed.' Al-Ḥākim recorded his aforementioned Hadith in al-Mustadrak.]]

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: It was read to Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā; Ibn Wahb informed us; ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed us; from Yaḥyā ibn Maymūn al-Ḥaḍramī, from Yūsuf ibn Tayraḥ: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "I have no knowledge." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked Jibrīl, and Jibrīl said: "I have no knowledge." Then Jibrīl asked an angel above him, and he said: "I have no knowledge." Then that angel asked his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, about what Jibrīl had asked him, which Muḥammad (ﷺ) had asked. The Lord, glorified and exalted, said: "He fulfilled the more righteous and the more lasting of them both, or he said: the purer of them both."[[Musnad al-Bazzār, no. 2245 (Kashf al-Astār).]]

This is mursal (a report in which the Successor omits the Companion from the chain), and it has come in a mursal form through another route. Sunayd said: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujāhid said: The Prophet (ﷺ) asked Jibrīl: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "I will ask Isrāfīl." So he asked him, and he said: "I will ask the Lord, Mighty and Majestic." So he asked Him, and He said: "He fulfilled the more righteous and the more complete of them both."[[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (20/44).]]

Another mursal route: Ibn Jarīr said: Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Abū Maʿshar narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazī, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "The more complete and the more perfect of them both."[[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (20/44).]]

These routes reinforce one another (mutaʿāḍidah). Moreover, it has been narrated as a marfūʿ (attributed to the Prophet) report from the narration of Abū Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Ḥāfiẓ Abū Bakr al-Bazzār said: Abū ʿUbaydillāh Yaḥyā ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Sakan narrated to us; Isḥāq ibn Idrīs narrated to us; ʿAwbad ibn Abī ʿImrān al-Jawnī narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ṣāmit, from Abū Dharr: that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "The more complete of them both and the more righteous of them both." He said: "And if you are asked which of the two women he married, then say: the younger of them."

Then al-Bazzār said: "We do not know of anything narrated from Abū Dharr except through this chain."[[Musnad al-Bazzār, no. 2244 (Kashf al-Astār).]]

Ibn Abī Ḥātim also narrated it from the Ḥadīth of ʿAwbad ibn Abī ʿImrān, who is ḍaʿīf (weak). Similar wording has also been narrated from the Ḥadīth of ʿUtbah ibn al-Nuddar [in some copies: al-Mundhir], with an extremely strange addition. Abū Bakr al-Bazzār said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb al-Sijistānī narrated to us; Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr narrated to us; Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us; al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Rabāḥ al-Lakhmī, who said: I heard ʿUtbah ibn al-Nuddar [in some copies: al-Mundhir] say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "The more righteous of them both and the more complete of them both." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When Mūsā, peace be upon him, wanted to part from Shuʿayb, peace be upon him, he instructed his wife to ask her father to give her some of his sheep on which they could live. So he gave her whatever his sheep bore that year of various colours. He said: Every ewe that passed, Mūsā struck its side with his staff, and they bore spotted offspring of all colours, and each ewe bore twins and triplets, none of them being fashūsh, nor ḍabūb, nor kamīshah that escapes the palm, nor thaʿūl." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you conquer al-Shām, you will indeed find remnants of them, and they are the Sāmiriyyah."[[Musnad al-Bazzār, no. 2246 (Kashf al-Astār).]]

This is how al-Bazzār reported it. Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated it in a fuller form than this, saying:

Abū Zurʿah narrated to us; Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Bukayr narrated to me; ʿAbdullāh ibn Lahīʿah narrated to me (ḥ). And Abū Zurʿah narrated to us; Ṣafwān narrated to us; al-Walīd narrated to us; ʿAbdullāh ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd al-Ḥaḍramī, from ʿAlī ibn Rabāḥ al-Lakhmī, who said: I heard ʿUtbah ibn al-Nudḍar [in some copies: al-Mundhir] al-Sulamī, the Companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), narrating that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Mūsā, peace be upon him, hired himself out in exchange for the chastity of his private part and the sustenance of his belly. When the term was fulfilled, it was said: O Messenger of Allah, which of the two terms? He said: The more righteous of them both and the more complete of them both. When he wanted to part from Shuʿayb, he instructed his wife to ask her father to give her some of his sheep on which they could live. So he gave her what his sheep bore of the colours of those born that year. His sheep were black and beautiful. Mūsā, peace be upon him, went to his staff, peeled it from its tip, then placed it at the lowest part of the trough, then brought the sheep and gave them drink, and Mūsā stood facing the trough. No ewe came out of it without him striking its side, ewe by ewe. He said: So they came into heat and conceived twice and thrice, and all of them bore various-coloured offspring, except one or two ewes, in which there was no fashūsh." Al-Walīd said: "Ḍabūn," and Ṣafwān said: "Ḍabūb." Abū Zurʿah said: "The correct form is ḍabūb, and neither ʿazūz, nor thaʿūl, nor kamīshah that escapes the palm." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "So if you conquer al-Shām, you will find remnants of those sheep, and they are the Sāmiriyyah."

And Abū Zurʿah narrated to us; Ṣafwān narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Walīd say: I asked Ibn Lahīʿah: What is the fashūsh? He said: The one that spills its milk, with a wide teat-opening. I said: What is the ḍabūb? He said: The one with a long udder that drags. I said: What is the ʿazūz? He said: The one with a narrow teat-opening. He said: What is the thaʿūl? He said: The one that has no udder except like two nipples. I said: What is the kamīshah? He said: The one that escapes the palm, having a small udder that the hand cannot grasp.

The core of this Ḥadīth rests on ʿAbdullāh ibn Lahīʿah al-Miṣrī, in whose memory there is weakness, and I fear that raising it to the Prophet (ﷺ) was an error, and Allah knows best. It should be narrated as "there is no fashūsh, no ʿazūz, no ḍabūb, no thaʿūl, and no kamīshah," so that each deficient attribute is mentioned together with its corresponding deficient attributes. Ibn Jarīr also narrated from the words of Anas ibn Mālik, as a statement attributed to him (mawqūf), something that approximates parts of this with a good chain. He said: Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us; Muʿādh ibn Hishām narrated to us; my father narrated to us, from Qatādah, who said: Anas ibn Mālik, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us: When the Prophet of Allah, Mūsā, peace be upon him, called his companion to the term that was between them, his companion said to him: "Every ewe that gives birth to a colour other than its own, that offspring is yours." So he went and set up poles over the water. When the ewes saw the shapes, they were frightened and wheeled around, and all of them gave birth to piebald (bulq) offspring, except one ewe. So he took their offspring away that year.[[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (20/44).]]

When the two women returned quickly with the sheep to their father, he noticed their unusual state and their quick return, so he asked them about their news. They told him what Musa (peace be upon him) had done. So he sent one of them to summon him to their father. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then one of them came to him walking shyly﴾, meaning walking like free women, as was narrated from the Commander of the Faithful, Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: she was concealed by the sleeve of her garment.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Narrated to us [my father, narrated to us] Abu Nu'aym, narrated to us Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Umar ibn Maymun, who said: Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: She came walking shyly, drawing her garment over her face, not brazen (safla') nor forward and loud-voiced (kharraja wa lajja). This is a sound chain (isnad).

Al-Jawhari said: As-salfa' among men means bold; among women, the forward and bold-tongued woman; among she-camels, the strong one.

﴿She said: Indeed my father invites you so that he may reward you with the wage for what you watered for us.﴾ This is an example of courtesy in speech. She did not request him in an absolute manner, lest it suggest doubt, but said: ﴿Indeed my father invites you so that he may reward you with the wage for what you watered for us﴾, meaning: so that he may recompense you and repay you for watering our sheep. ﴿So when he came to him and related the narrative﴾, meaning: he told him what had happened to him and the cause for which he had left his land. ﴿He said: Fear not; you have escaped from the wrongdoing people.﴾ He means: be at ease and let your eye be comforted, for you have left their kingdom, so they have no authority in our lands. For this reason he said: ﴿You have escaped from the wrongdoing people.﴾

The exegetes differed about who this man was, with several opinions. One is that he was Shu'ayb the Prophet (peace be upon him), who was sent to the people of Madyan. This is the well-known view of many, and it was said by al-Hasan al-Basri and others. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Narrated to us my father, narrated to us Abd al-Aziz al-Uwaysi, narrated to us Malik ibn Anas: that it reached him that Shu'ayb is the one to whom Musa related the narrative, and he said: ﴿Fear not; you have escaped from the wrongdoing people.﴾

al-Tabarani narrated from Salama ibn Sa'd al-Anazi that he came as a delegation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said to him: "Welcome to the people of Shu'ayb and the sisters of Musa; you have been guided."

Others said: rather he was the nephew of Shu'ayb. It was also said: he was a believing man from the people of Shu'ayb. And others said: Shu'ayb lived a long time before the time of Musa (peace be upon him), because he said to his people: ﴿And the people of Lut are not far from you﴾ [Hud: 89]. The destruction of the people of Lut occurred in the time of the Friend (al-Khalil, Ibrahim) (peace be upon him), by the text of the Qur'an, and it is known that between Musa and al-Khalil, peace be upon them both, there was a long period exceeding four hundred years, as mentioned by more than one scholar. As for what was said, that Shu'ayb lived a long time, that is—and Allah knows best—a way of avoiding this difficulty. Then, among the indications that he is not Shu'ayb is that, had he been him, the Qur'an would likely have explicitly named him here. What has come in some hadiths explicitly mentioning him in the story of Musa has no sound chain, as we will mention shortly, Allah willing. Then, among what is found in the books of the Children of Israel, this man's name is "Tharun" (Thibrun), and Allah knows best.

Abu Ubayda ibn Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: Athrun, and he is the nephew of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him).

And from Abu Hamza, from Ibn Abbas: The one who hired Musa was Yathra, the lord of Madyan. Ibn Jarir narrated it, then said: The correct view is that this cannot be known except by a report, and there is no report by which proof is established regarding this.

* *

His saying: ﴿One of the two said: O my father, hire him; indeed the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.﴾ That is, one of the two daughters of this man said it. It was said: she is the one who went after Musa, peace be upon him, and she said to her father: ﴿O my father, hire him﴾, meaning: to tend this flock.

Umar, Ibn Abbas, Shurayh al-Qadi, Abu Malik, Qatada, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, and others said: When she said: ﴿Indeed the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy﴾, her father said to her: "And how do you know that?" She said: "He lifted the stone which no more than ten men could lift, and when I came with him, I walked ahead of him; he said to me: 'Be behind me, and if I deviate from the path, throw a pebble so I may know the way, that I may be guided by it.'"

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Ubayda, from Abdullah, that is Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The most perceptive of people are three: Abu Bakr, when he perceived in Umar; the companion of Yusuf, when he said: ﴿Make his residence honorable﴾ [Yusuf: 21]; and the companion of Musa, when she said: ﴿O my father, hire him; indeed the best one you can hire is the strong, the trustworthy.﴾

He said: ﴿Indeed I intend to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine﴾, meaning: this elderly old man asked him to tend his sheep and to marry him to one of his two daughters.

* *

His saying, the Exalted, reporting about Musa (peace be upon him): ﴿He said: That is between me and you; whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there shall be no injustice against me; and Allah is Witness over what we say.﴾ He means: Musa said to his father-in-law: The matter is as you have said, that you hired me for eight years, and if I complete ten, it is from me. Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Marwan ibn Shuja' narrated to us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A Jew from the people of al-Hira asked me: "Which of the two terms did Musa fulfill?"
