In the "Hadith of the Trials" narrated by al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, it occurs that the one who asked him was a man from the Christians. The first is more correct, and Allah knows best. It has also been narrated through mursal chains from a hadith of Ibn Abbas raised to the Prophet (ﷺ). Ibn Jarir said:

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi narrated to us, al-Humaydi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Abi Ya'qub narrated to me, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I asked Jibril: 'Which of the two terms did Musa fulfill?' He said: 'The more complete and the more perfect of them.'" [Tafsir al-Tabari (20/44)].

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, from his father, from al-Humaydi, from Sufyan, that is Ibn Uyayna, who said: Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Abi Ya'qub narrated to me, and he was one of my elders or younger than me, and he mentioned it.

I say: This Ibrahim is not well known.

The Hadith narrated by al-Bazzar from Ahmad ibn Abān al-Qurashī, from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, from Ibrāhīm ibn Aʿyan, from al-Ḥakam ibn Abān, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with the same wording as above. He then said: "We do not know it to be attributed to the Prophet (ﷺ) through Ibn ʿAbbās except through this route."[[Al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar said in Lisān al-Mīzān (1/124): "Ibrāhīm ibn Yaḥyā al-ʿAdanī, from al-Ḥakam ibn Abān, and from him Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, with a munkar report, and the man is unknown (nakirah). His narration from al-Ḥumaydī, and its text: The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked, and Jibrīl (peace be upon him) [was asked] which of the two terms Mūsā fulfilled." End of quote. Ibn Ḥibbān mentioned this man in al-Thiqāt. Al-Azdī said: 'His narration is not followed.' Al-Ḥākim recorded his aforementioned Hadith in al-Mustadrak.]]

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: It was read to Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā; Ibn Wahb informed us; ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith informed us; from Yaḥyā ibn Maymūn al-Ḥaḍramī, from Yūsuf ibn Tayraḥ: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "I have no knowledge." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked Jibrīl, and Jibrīl said: "I have no knowledge." Then Jibrīl asked an angel above him, and he said: "I have no knowledge." Then that angel asked his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, about what Jibrīl had asked him, which Muḥammad (ﷺ) had asked. The Lord, glorified and exalted, said: "He fulfilled the more righteous and the more lasting of them both, or he said: the purer of them both."[[Musnad al-Bazzār, no. 2245 (Kashf al-Astār).]]

This is mursal (a report in which the Successor omits the Companion from the chain), and it has come in a mursal form through another route. Sunayd said: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujāhid said: The Prophet (ﷺ) asked Jibrīl: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "I will ask Isrāfīl." So he asked him, and he said: "I will ask the Lord, Mighty and Majestic." So he asked Him, and He said: "He fulfilled the more righteous and the more complete of them both."[[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (20/44).]]

Another mursal route: Ibn Jarīr said: Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Abū Maʿshar narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazī, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "The more complete and the more perfect of them both."[[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (20/44).]]

These routes reinforce one another (mutaʿāḍidah). Moreover, it has been narrated as a marfūʿ (attributed to the Prophet) report from the narration of Abū Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Ḥāfiẓ Abū Bakr al-Bazzār said: Abū ʿUbaydillāh Yaḥyā ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Sakan narrated to us; Isḥāq ibn Idrīs narrated to us; ʿAwbad ibn Abī ʿImrān al-Jawnī narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ṣāmit, from Abū Dharr: that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "The more complete of them both and the more righteous of them both." He said: "And if you are asked which of the two women he married, then say: the younger of them."

Then al-Bazzār said: "We do not know of anything narrated from Abū Dharr except through this chain."[[Musnad al-Bazzār, no. 2244 (Kashf al-Astār).]]

Ibn Abī Ḥātim also narrated it from the Ḥadīth of ʿAwbad ibn Abī ʿImrān, who is ḍaʿīf (weak). Similar wording has also been narrated from the Ḥadīth of ʿUtbah ibn al-Nuddar [in some copies: al-Mundhir], with an extremely strange addition. Abū Bakr al-Bazzār said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb al-Sijistānī narrated to us; Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr narrated to us; Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us; al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Rabāḥ al-Lakhmī, who said: I heard ʿUtbah ibn al-Nuddar [in some copies: al-Mundhir] say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Which of the two terms did Mūsā fulfil?" He said: "The more righteous of them both and the more complete of them both." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When Mūsā, peace be upon him, wanted to part from Shuʿayb, peace be upon him, he instructed his wife to ask her father to give her some of his sheep on which they could live. So he gave her whatever his sheep bore that year of various colours. He said: Every ewe that passed, Mūsā struck its side with his staff, and they bore spotted offspring of all colours, and each ewe bore twins and triplets, none of them being fashūsh, nor ḍabūb, nor kamīshah that escapes the palm, nor thaʿūl." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you conquer al-Shām, you will indeed find remnants of them, and they are the Sāmiriyyah."[[Musnad al-Bazzār, no. 2246 (Kashf al-Astār).]]

This is how al-Bazzār reported it. Ibn Abī Ḥātim narrated it in a fuller form than this, saying:

Abū Zurʿah narrated to us; Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbdullāh ibn Bukayr narrated to me; ʿAbdullāh ibn Lahīʿah narrated to me (ḥ). And Abū Zurʿah narrated to us; Ṣafwān narrated to us; al-Walīd narrated to us; ʿAbdullāh ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us, from al-Ḥārith ibn Yazīd al-Ḥaḍramī, from ʿAlī ibn Rabāḥ al-Lakhmī, who said: I heard ʿUtbah ibn al-Nudḍar [in some copies: al-Mundhir] al-Sulamī, the Companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), narrating that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Mūsā, peace be upon him, hired himself out in exchange for the chastity of his private part and the sustenance of his belly. When the term was fulfilled, it was said: O Messenger of Allah, which of the two terms? He said: The more righteous of them both and the more complete of them both. When he wanted to part from Shuʿayb, he instructed his wife to ask her father to give her some of his sheep on which they could live. So he gave her what his sheep bore of the colours of those born that year. His sheep were black and beautiful. Mūsā, peace be upon him, went to his staff, peeled it from its tip, then placed it at the lowest part of the trough, then brought the sheep and gave them drink, and Mūsā stood facing the trough. No ewe came out of it without him striking its side, ewe by ewe. He said: So they came into heat and conceived twice and thrice, and all of them bore various-coloured offspring, except one or two ewes, in which there was no fashūsh." Al-Walīd said: "Ḍabūn," and Ṣafwān said: "Ḍabūb." Abū Zurʿah said: "The correct form is ḍabūb, and neither ʿazūz, nor thaʿūl, nor kamīshah that escapes the palm." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "So if you conquer al-Shām, you will find remnants of those sheep, and they are the Sāmiriyyah."

And Abū Zurʿah narrated to us; Ṣafwān narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Walīd say: I asked Ibn Lahīʿah: What is the fashūsh? He said: The one that spills its milk, with a wide teat-opening. I said: What is the ḍabūb? He said: The one with a long udder that drags. I said: What is the ʿazūz? He said: The one with a narrow teat-opening. He said: What is the thaʿūl? He said: The one that has no udder except like two nipples. I said: What is the kamīshah? He said: The one that escapes the palm, having a small udder that the hand cannot grasp.

The core of this Ḥadīth rests on ʿAbdullāh ibn Lahīʿah al-Miṣrī, in whose memory there is weakness, and I fear that raising it to the Prophet (ﷺ) was an error, and Allah knows best. It should be narrated as "there is no fashūsh, no ʿazūz, no ḍabūb, no thaʿūl, and no kamīshah," so that each deficient attribute is mentioned together with its corresponding deficient attributes. Ibn Jarīr also narrated from the words of Anas ibn Mālik, as a statement attributed to him (mawqūf), something that approximates parts of this with a good chain. He said: Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us; Muʿādh ibn Hishām narrated to us; my father narrated to us, from Qatādah, who said: Anas ibn Mālik, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us: When the Prophet of Allah, Mūsā, peace be upon him, called his companion to the term that was between them, his companion said to him: "Every ewe that gives birth to a colour other than its own, that offspring is yours." So he went and set up poles over the water. When the ewes saw the shapes, they were frightened and wheeled around, and all of them gave birth to piebald (bulq) offspring, except one ewe. So he took their offspring away that year.[[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (20/44).]]

The Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 28, verses 29–32:

It has already been mentioned in the tafsir of the verse before it that Musa (peace be upon him) fulfilled the better and more complete of the two terms, the fullest, the most righteous, the most perfect and the most pure of them. This is also derived from the noble verse in His saying [in A: "where He said"]: ﴿So when Musa had fulfilled the term﴾, meaning the more complete of the two. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid: "He fulfilled ten years, and then ten more." I have not seen this view attributed to anyone else, though Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim have transmitted it from him. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And he set out with his family﴾, they said: Musa had longed for his land and his family, so he resolved to visit them secretly, away from Fir'awn and his people. He loaded his family and the sheep that his father-in-law had given him, and he travelled with them on a rainy, dark, cold night. He halted at a station, and every time he struck his firestone it would not produce any light. He wondered at this, and while he was in that state ﴿he saw from the side of the Mount a fire﴾, meaning he saw a fire shining for him from a distance. ﴿He said to his family: "Stay here, indeed I have seen a fire"﴾, meaning: until I go to it. ﴿"Perhaps I may bring you from it some news"﴾. That was because he had lost the way. ﴿"Or a brand from the fire, that you may warm yourselves"﴾, meaning a piece of it, ﴿"that you may warm yourselves"﴾, meaning that you may warm yourselves from the cold with it.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley﴾, meaning from the side of the valley on his right, near the mountain, from the direction of the west, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And you were not on the western side when We decreed the command to Musa﴾. This indicates that Musa approached the fire facing the direction of the qiblah, with the western mountain on his right. He found the fire blazing in a green tree in the foot of the mountain beside the valley, so he stood bewildered by it. Then his Lord called him: ﴿from the right side of the valley, in the blessed spot, from the tree﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn WakI' narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abdullah, who said: "I saw the tree from which Musa, peace be upon him, was called: it was a green acacia, fresh and luxuriant." Its chain is close (to sound).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from some of those who are not accused, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: "It was a tree of al-'Ulayq." Some of the People of the Book say it was of al-'Awsaj.

Qatadah said: "It was of al-'Awsaj, and his staff was of al-'Awsaj."

* *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿"O Musa, indeed I am Allah, the Lord of the worlds"﴾, meaning: the One who is speaking to you and addressing you is the Lord of the worlds, the Doer of what He wills, there is no god but Him and no lord besides Him, exalted, sanctified and far removed from resemblance to His creation in His essence, His attributes, His sayings and His deeds, glory be to Him!

* *

As for His saying: ﴿"And throw down your staff"﴾, meaning: the one that is in your hand, as He confirmed it when He said: ﴿"And what is that in your right hand, O Musa?" He said, "It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I beat down [leaves] with it for my sheep, and I have in it other uses"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 17, 18]. The meaning is: "This is your staff that you know; throw it down." ﴿So he threw it down, and suddenly it was a snake, moving swiftly﴾. Thus he knew and was certain that the One who was speaking to him and addressing him is the One who says to a thing "Be," and it is. This explanation has already been given in Surah Ta-Ha.

And here He said: ﴿So when he saw it moving﴾, meaning writhing, ﴿as if it were a jann﴾, meaning in its swift movement together with the great size of its body, the wideness of its mouth, and the clashing of its fangs and molars, so that it would not pass by a rock without swallowing it, and it would go down into its mouth crunching, as if it were a stone rolling in a valley. At that, ﴿he turned back fleeing and did not look back﴾, meaning he did not turn around, because human nature recoils from such a thing. When Allah said to him: ﴿"O Musa, come forward and do not fear; indeed you are among the secure"﴾, he returned and stood in his first position.

Then Allah said to him: ﴿"Insert your hand into your pocket; it will come out white without harm"﴾, meaning: when you put your hand into the pocket of your garment and then take it out, it will come out shining like a piece of the moon, in the brilliance of lightning. Therefore He said: ﴿"without harm"﴾, meaning without leprosy.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿"And draw your arm close to your side from fear"﴾. Mujahid said: "From fright." Qatadah said: "From terror." 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam and Ibn Jarir said: "From what befell you of fear of the serpent."

The apparent meaning is more general than this: that he was commanded, whenever he feared something, to draw his wing to himself from fear, meaning his hand. When he does this, what he feels of fear departs from him. And perhaps when anyone follows this example by placing his hands upon his heart, what he feels will leave him or lessen, if Allah wills; and in Him is trust.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, al-Rabi' ibn Tha'lab, the righteous shaykh, narrated to us, Abu Isma'il al-Mu'addib informed us, from 'Abdullah ibn Muslim, from Mujahid, who said: "Musa, peace be upon him, had his heart filled with terror of Fir'awn, so whenever he saw him he would say: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You against his throat, and I seek refuge in You from his evil.' So Allah removed what was in the heart of Musa, peace be upon him, and placed it in the heart of Fir'awn, so whenever he saw him he would urinate as a donkey urinates."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿"These two are proofs from your Lord to Fir'awn and his chiefs"﴾, meaning: his throwing down the staff and its becoming a snake moving swiftly, and his inserting his hand into his pocket so that it comes out white without harm, are two decisive and clear proofs of the power of the Free Chooser and of the validity of the prophethood of the one upon whose hands this extraordinary sign occurred. Therefore He said: ﴿"to Fir'awn and his chiefs"﴾, meaning his people among the leaders, the great ones and the followers. ﴿"Indeed they were a people of defiance"﴾, meaning: they were out of obedience to Allah, opposing the religion of Allah. [And Allah knows best.]

As for His saying: ﴿"And throw down your staff"﴾, meaning: the one that is in your hand, as He confirmed it when He said: ﴿"And what is that in your right hand, O Musa?" The meaning is: "This is your staff that you know; throw it down." ﴿So he threw it down, and suddenly it was a snake, moving swiftly﴾. And here He said: ﴿So when he saw it moving﴾, meaning writhing, ﴿as if it were a jann﴾, meaning in its swift movement together with the great size of its body, the wideness of its mouth, and the clashing of its fangs and molars, so that it would not pass by a rock without swallowing it, and it would go down into its mouth crunching, as if it were a stone rolling in a valley. * *

The apparent meaning is more general than this: that he was commanded, whenever he feared something, to draw his wing to himself from fear, meaning his hand. When he does this, what he feels of fear departs from him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, al-Rabi' ibn Tha'lab, the righteous shaykh, narrated to us, Abu Isma'il al-Mu'addib informed us, from 'Abdullah ibn Muslim, from Mujahid, who said: "Musa, peace be upon him, had his heart filled with terror of Fir'awn, so whenever he saw him he would say: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You against his throat, and I seek refuge in You from his evil.' [And Allah knows best.]

The Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 28, verses 29–32:

It has already been mentioned in the tafsir of the verse before it that Musa (peace be upon him) fulfilled the better and more complete of the two terms, the fullest, the most righteous, the most perfect and the most pure of them. This is also derived from the noble verse in His saying [in A: "where He said"]: ﴿So when Musa had fulfilled the term﴾, meaning the more complete of the two. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Najih narrated from Mujahid: "He fulfilled ten years, and then ten more." I have not seen this view attributed to anyone else, though Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim have transmitted it from him. And Allah knows best.

* *

He halted at a station, and every time he struck his firestone it would not produce any light. He wondered at this, and while he was in that state ﴿he saw from the side of the Mount a fire﴾, meaning he saw a fire shining for him from a distance. ﴿He said to his family: "Stay here, indeed I have seen a fire"﴾, meaning: until I go to it. ﴿"Perhaps I may bring you from it some news"﴾. That was because he had lost the way. ﴿"Or a brand from the fire, that you may warm yourselves"﴾, meaning a piece of it, ﴿"that you may warm yourselves"﴾, meaning that you may warm yourselves from the cold with it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from some of those who are not accused, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: "It was a tree of al-'Ulayq." Some of the People of the Book say it was of al-'Awsaj.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 28, verse 33–35:

When Allah commanded him to go to Pharaoh, who had driven him out of the land of Egypt in flight from him and in fear of his tyranny, he said: ﴿My Lord, I killed a person among them, so I fear they will kill me﴾, meaning: that Qibti (Coptic man). ﴿So I fear that they will kill me﴾, i.e., if they see me.

﴿And my brother Harun (Aaron), he is more eloquent in tongue than I﴾. That is because Musa, peace be upon him, had a speech impediment (lathgah) in his tongue, due to what he had taken from that ember when he was given the choice between it and the date or the pearl. He took the ember and placed it on his tongue, and so there remained a difficulty in his expression. Therefore he said: ﴿And loosen the knot from my tongue, that they may understand my speech. And appoint for me a minister from my family, Harun, my brother. Strengthen through him my back, and let him share my task﴾ [Ta-Ha: 27–32]. That is: let him be a companion to me in what You have commanded me of this great station, which is bearing the burdens of prophethood and messengership to this arrogant, tyrannical, obstinate king. Therefore he said: ﴿And my brother Harun, he is more eloquent in tongue than I, so send him with me as a supporter [who will confirm me]﴾ [[Addition from t.]], i.e., a minister, helper and one who strengthens my cause, confirming what I say and what I report from Allah, Mighty and Majestic; for the report of two is more effective upon souls than the report of one. Therefore he said: ﴿Indeed, I fear that they will deny me﴾.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: ﴿A supporter who confirms me﴾, i.e., he explains to them on my behalf what I speak to them about, for he understands [on my behalf] [[Addition from a.]].

When he asked for that, Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿We will strengthen your arm through your brother﴾, i.e., We will strengthen your affair and exalt your side through your brother, whom you asked to be a prophet with you. As He said in another verse: ﴿You have been granted your request, O Musa﴾ [Ta-Ha: 36], and the Exalted said: ﴿And We gave him, out of Our mercy, his brother Harun as a prophet﴾ [Maryam: 53]. Therefore some of the early scholars said: No one has a greater favor upon his brother than Musa upon Harun, peace be upon them both, for he interceded for him until Allah made him a prophet and messenger with him to Pharaoh and his chiefs. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, said concerning Musa: ﴿And he was, in the sight of Allah, distinguished﴾ [al-Ahzab: 69].

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We will give you both authority﴾, i.e., a overpowering proof, ﴿so they will not reach you both by Our signs﴾, i.e., there will be no way for them to reach you both to harm you because of your conveying the signs of Allah, as Allah, the Exalted, said to His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord [And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message], and Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67] [[Addition from t., a; in h: "up to his saying"]]. And the Exalted said: ﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him and fear none except Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner﴾ [al-Ahzab: 39], i.e., sufficient is Allah as helper, supporter and confirmer. Therefore He informed them both that the final outcome is theirs, and for those who follow them, in this world and the Hereafter, so He said: ﴿You both and whoever follows you will be the victorious﴾, as the Exalted said: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers." Indeed, Allah is Strong and Mighty﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 21], and the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believed in the worldly life and on the day when the witnesses stand. The day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse and for them is the evil home﴾ [Ghafir: 51–52].

Ibn Jarir gave the interpretation that the meaning is: ﴿And We will give you both authority, so they will not reach you both﴾, then he begins: ﴿By Our signs, you both and whoever follows you will be the victorious﴾, its estimated sense being: You both and whoever follows you will be the victorious by Our signs [[Tafsir al-Tabari (20/48).]].

There is no doubt that this meaning is correct, and it is attained from the first interpretation, so there is no need for this, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 28, verses 36–37:

He, exalted is He, informs about the coming of Musa and his brother Harun to Fir'awn and his chieftains, and their presenting to them what Allah had given them of striking miracles and compelling proofs, as evidence of their truthfulness in what they reported from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, concerning His Oneness and the obligation to follow His commands. When Fir'awn and his chieftains witnessed that, saw it, verified it, and were certain that it was from Allah, they turned, in their disbelief and transgression, to obstinacy and bafflement. That was due to their arrogance and their pride in refusing to follow the truth. So they said: ﴿This is nothing but fabricated magic﴾, i.e., invented and manufactured. They also intended to counter him through trickery and (worldly) standing, but that did not avail them.

* *

As for His saying [[In manuscripts T and F: "And their saying."]]: ﴿And we did not hear of this among our earlier fathers﴾, they mean: the worship of Allah alone, with no partner for Him. They say: we have not seen any of our fathers upon this religion, and we have not seen the people except associating other gods with Allah. Then Musa, peace be upon him, replied to them: ﴿My Lord knows best who has come with guidance from Him﴾, meaning: between me and you, and He will judge between me and you. For this reason He said: ﴿and to whom will belong the ultimate outcome of the abode﴾, i.e., victory, triumph and support. ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾, i.e., those who associate partners with Allah.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) reports that Allah, exalted is He, speaks of the disbelief, tyranny and fabrication of Pharaoh (may Allah curse him) in claiming divinity for himself, an ugly claim, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So he made his people light-headed, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 54]. That is because he called them to acknowledge his divinity, and they responded to him out of the feebleness of their minds and the shallowness of their understanding. Hence he said: ﴿O assembly, I know of no god for you other than me﴾, [and] [[Addition from manuscripts T and F.]] Allah the Exalted said, relating about him: ﴿Then he gathered [his people] and called out, and said, "I am your lord, the most high." So Allah seized him in the punishment of the Hereafter and the first [life]. Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears﴾ [An-Nazi'at: 23-26]. That is, he gathered his people, called out to them with his loud voice, declaring this plainly to them, and they responded to him, listening and obeying. Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on surah 28, verse 43:

He, may He be exalted, informs of the favour He bestowed upon His servant and messenger Musa (Moses) the Speaker (al-Kalim), upon whom be prayers and peace from his Lord, in sending down the Tawrah (Torah) to him after He had destroyed Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and his chiefs.

* *

His saying: ﴿After We had destroyed the earlier generations﴾ means: after the revelation of the Torah, He did not punish a nation with a general punishment, but commanded the believers to fight the enemies of Allah among the polytheists, as He said: ﴿And Fir'awn and those before him and the overturned cities brought wrongdoing. They disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with a severe seizing﴾ [al-Haqqah: 9, 10].

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Muhammad and 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, both saying: 'Awf narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: "Allah did not destroy any people with a punishment from the sky or from the earth after the Torah was sent down upon the face of the earth, except the town whose people were transformed into apes. Do you not see that Allah says: ﴿And We certainly gave Musa the Scripture after We had destroyed the earlier generations﴾?" [Tafsir al-Tabari (20/50).]

Ibn Abi Hatim related it with similar wording from the hadith of 'Awf ibn Abi Jamilah [in A: "Habilah"] al-A'rabi. Abu Bakr al-Bazzar also related it in his Musnad, from 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas, from Yahya al-Qattan, from 'Awf, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, as a statement of his own (mawquf). Then he related it from Nasr ibn 'Ali, from 'Abd al-A'la, from 'Awf, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, traced back (rafa'ahu) to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah did not destroy any people with a punishment from the sky or from the earth except before Musa." Then he recited: ﴿And We certainly gave Musa the Scripture after We had destroyed the earlier generations﴾ [Musnad al-Bazzar no. 2248, Kashf al-Astar; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/88): "al-Bazzar related it as mawquf and as marfu', and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

* *

His saying: ﴿As insights for the people﴾ means: from blindness and error. ﴿And guidance﴾ to the truth. ﴿And mercy﴾ means: guidance toward righteous deeds. ﴿That they might remember﴾ means: that people may remember by it and be guided through it.

The passage begins with Allah, exalted is He, drawing attention to the proof of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, in that he reported unseen events of the past in such a way that the one who hears it would think he was a witness to what had preceded. He was an unlettered man who could not read any of the Scriptures, raised among a people who knew nothing of that. Likewise, when He informed him about Maryam and what happened to her, Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And you were not with them when they cast their pens [to decide] which of them would be entrusted with Maryam, nor were you with them when they disputed﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 44], meaning: you were not present for that, but Allah revealed it to you. Similarly, when He informed him about Nuh and his people, and what Allah did in saving him and drowning his people.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿These are among the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. You knew them not, neither you nor your people, before this. So be patient; indeed the good outcome is for the righteous﴾ [Hud: 49]. He also said at the end of the surah: ﴿That is among the news of the towns which We relate to you﴾ [Hud: 100]. And after mentioning the story of Yusuf, He said: ﴿That is among the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, and you were not with them when they resolved on their plan while they were scheming﴾ [Yusuf: 102]. In Surat Ta-Ha He said: ﴿Thus do We relate to you the news of what has passed, and We have given you from Us a reminder﴾ [Ta-Ha: 99]. And here, after He had reported the story of Musa from its beginning to its end, and how the beginning of Allah's revelation to him and His speaking to him occurred, He said: ﴿And you were not on the western side when We decreed to Musa the command﴾. That is, O Muhammad, you were not at the western side of the mountain where Allah spoke to Musa from the tree which is on the eastern side of the valley's shore, ﴿nor were you among the witnesses﴾ to that. But Allah, glorified and exalted is He, revealed that to you, so that it would be a proof and evidence against generations whose time had grown long, who had forgotten the proofs of Allah against them and what He had revealed to the earlier prophets.

* *

His saying: ﴿And you were not dwelling among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses﴾ means: you were not residing among the people of Madyan reciting to them Our verses, when you reported about their prophet Shu'ayb, what he said to his people, and what they replied to him. ﴿But We were sending [messengers]﴾ means: but We revealed that to you, and We sent you to mankind as a messenger.

﴿And you were not at the side of the Mount when We called out﴾. Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i said in the book of tafsir from his Sunan: Ali ibn Hujr informed us, Isa — and he is Ibn Yunus — informed us, from Hamzah al-Zayyat, from al-A'mash, from Ali ibn Mudrik, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, [regarding] ﴿And you were not at the side of the Mount when We called out﴾, he said: "They were called: O nation of Muhammad, I gave you before you asked Me, and I answered you before you called upon Me."

Similarly Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of a group, from Hamzah — and he is Ibn Habib al-Zayyat — from al-A'mash. Ibn Jarir also narrated it from the hadith of Waki' and Yahya ibn Isa, from al-A'mash, from Ali ibn Mudrik, from Abu Zur'ah — and he is Ibn 'Amr ibn Jarir [[Tafsir al-Tabari (20/51), where it is through the chain of Sufyan and Yahya ibn Isa.]] — that he said this as part of his own speech, and Allah knows best.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: ﴿And you were not at the side of the Mount when We called out﴾: [it refers to] your ummah in the loins of their fathers, that they would believe in you when you were sent.

Qatadah said: ﴿And you were not at the side of the Mount when We called out﴾ [refers to] Musa. This, and Allah knows best, is more similar to His saying: ﴿And you were not on the western side when We decreed to Musa the command﴾.

Then here He reported with another, more specific form, which is the calling out (al-nida'), as He said: ﴿And when your Lord called out to Musa﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 10], and He said: ﴿When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 16], and He said: ﴿And We called to him from the right side of the Mount and brought him near in confidence﴾ [Maryam: 52].

* *

His saying: ﴿But it is a mercy from your Lord﴾ means: you were not witnessing any of that, but Allah revealed it to you and informed you of it, as a mercy from Him to you and to the servants by sending you to them, ﴿that you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you, that they might remember﴾, meaning: that they might be guided by what you brought them from Allah, mighty and majestic is He.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 28, verses 48–51:

He, exalted is He, says, informing about the people who, if He had punished them before the proof was established against them, would have argued that no messenger had come to them. When the truth came to them from Him through Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, they said, out of obstinacy, opposition, disbelief, ignorance and heresy: ﴿Why was he not given the like of what Moses was given? Did they not disbelieve in what Moses was given before?﴾ They meant, and Allah knows best: the many signs, such as the staff and the hand, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood, and the reduction of crops and fruits, which afflicted the enemies of Allah; and the splitting of the sea, the shading of the clouds, and the sending down of the manna and the quails, and other striking signs and overpowering proofs, which Allah brought about through the hands of Moses, peace be upon him, as evidence and proofs for him against Pharaoh, his chiefs and the Children of Israel. Despite all of this, it did not benefit Pharaoh and his chiefs; rather, they disbelieved in Moses and his brother Aaron, as they said to them both: ﴿Have you come to us to turn us away from what we found our fathers following, and so that you two may have greatness in the land? We are not believers in you two.﴾ [Yunus: 78]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So they denied them both, and they were among the destroyed.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 48].

Therefore He says here: ﴿Did they not disbelieve in what Moses was given before?﴾, meaning: Did mankind not disbelieve in what Moses was given of those great signs? ﴿They said: Two sorcerers supporting each other,﴾ meaning, cooperating, ﴿and they said: Indeed we are disbelievers in both of them,﴾ meaning: we disbelieve in each of them. Because of the strength of their association, companionship and pairing, the mention of one of Moses and Aaron indicates the other, as the poet said:

"I do not know, when I set out for a land seeking good, which of the two will meet me..."

meaning: I do not know whether good or evil will meet me.

Mujahid ibn Jabr said: The Jews instructed the Quraysh to say this to Muhammad, ﷺ, so Allah said: ﴿Did they not disbelieve in what Moses was given before? They said: Two sorcerers supporting each other.﴾ He said: meaning Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them. ﴿Supporting each other﴾ means: cooperating and aiding each other, and each of them confirmed the other. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Abu Razin said likewise concerning His words ﴿two sorcerers﴾, meaning Moses and Aaron. This is a good and strong opinion, and Allah knows best.

Muslim ibn Yasar related from Ibn Abbas: ﴿They said: Two sorcerers supporting each other﴾, meaning Moses and Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them both. This is also a narration from al-Hasan al-Basri.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: meaning Jesus and Muhammad, may Allah bless them both and grant them peace. This is distant, because Jesus has not been mentioned at all here, and Allah knows best.

As for those who read ﴿sihran (two sorcerers)﴾ [the reading with the verb form], Ali ibn Abi Talhah and al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas: they meant the Tawrah (Torah) and the Qur'an. Likewise said 'Asim al-Jahdari, al-Suddi, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. al-Suddi said: meaning each of them confirmed the other.

Ikrimah said: they meant the Tawrah and the Injil (Gospel). This is a narration from Abu Zur'ah, and Ibn Jarir chose it.

al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: the Injil and the Qur'an. Allah, glorified is He, knows the correct view. Apparently, according to the reading ﴿sihran﴾, they meant the Tawrah and the Qur'an, because He said after it: ﴿Say: Then bring a Book from Allah that is better guided than these two, and I will follow it, if you are truthful.﴾ Allah often pairs the Tawrah with the Qur'an, as in His saying: ﴿Say: Who sent down the Book which Moses brought as a light and guidance for mankind?﴾ up to His words ﴿And this is a blessed Book which We have sent down﴾ [al-An'am: 91, 92], and He said at the end of the surah: ﴿Then We gave Moses the Book, complete upon the one who did good﴾ up to His words ﴿And this is a blessed Book which We have sent down, so follow it and fear Allah that you may receive mercy﴾ [al-An'am: 155]. And the jinn said: ﴿Indeed we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what came before it﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30]. [Addition from A.] Waraqah ibn Nawfal said: "This is the Namus (the revealed law/angel of revelation) that was sent down to Moses." It is known necessarily to people of understanding that Allah has not sent down from heaven, among the many books He revealed to His prophets, any book more perfect, more comprehensive, more eloquent, greater, or more noble than the Book revealed to Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, which is the Qur'an. After it in nobility and greatness is the Book which He revealed to Moses son of Imran, peace be upon him, which is the Tawrah, about which Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed We sent down the Tawrah, in which is guidance and light, by which the prophets who submitted judged for those who were Jews, and the rabbis and the scholars, by what they were entrusted with of the Book of Allah, and they were witnesses over it.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 44]. The Injil was revealed only to complete the Tawrah and to make lawful some of what had been forbidden to the Children of Israel. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: Then bring a Book from Allah that is better guided than these two, and I will follow it, if you are truthful﴾, meaning: in what you use to argue against the truth and oppose falsehood with.

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿But if they do not respond to you﴾, meaning: if they do not answer you concerning what you have said to them and do not follow the truth, ﴿then know that they only follow their own desires﴾, meaning: without any proof or argument. ﴿And who is more astray than one who follows his desire without guidance from Allah﴾, meaning: without a proof taken from the Book of Allah. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We have certainly conveyed to them the word﴾, Mujahid said: We have explained to them the word. al-Suddi said: We have made the word clear to them.

Qatadah said: He, exalted is He, says: He informed them how He dealt with those who passed before, and how He will deal with them, ﴿that perhaps they will remember﴾.

Mujahid and others said: ﴿We have conveyed to them﴾ refers to the Quraysh. This is the apparent meaning. However, Hammad ibn Salamah related from Amr ibn Dinar, from Yahya ibn Ja'dah, from Rifa'ah (this Rifa'ah is Ibn Qaraẓah al-Quraẓi; Ibn Mandah made him Rifa'ah ibn Samaw'al, maternal uncle of Safiyyah bint Huyayy, and he is the one who divorced Tamimah bint Wahb, whom Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Zubayr ibn Batta married after him, as Ibn al-Athir mentioned), who said: ﴿And We have certainly conveyed to them the word﴾ was revealed concerning ten people, of whom I am one. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through him. [Tafsir al-Tabari (20/56); al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (5/53) through the chain of Hammad ibn Salamah.]

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says: Allah the Exalted informs about the scholars (al-'ulama') among the People of the Book who are (al-awliya', "the close allies/adherents") that they believe in the Qur'an, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book recite it as it should be recited; those believe in it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 121], and He says: ﴿And among the People of the Book are those who believe in Allah and in what has been revealed to you and what has been revealed to them, humbly submissive to Allah﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 199], and He says: ﴿Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall prostrate on their faces in prostration, and say, "Glory be to our Lord! Indeed the promise of our Lord is ever fulfilled."﴾ [al-Isra': 107-108], and He says: ﴿You will surely find the nearest of them in affection to those who believe are those who say, "We are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant. And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses."﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 82-83].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It was revealed concerning seventy of the priests (al-qissisin) whom the Negus (al-Najashi) sent. When they came to the Prophet ﷺ, he recited to them: ﴿Ya-Sin. By the wise Qur'an﴾ until he finished the surah, and they began to weep and embraced Islam. And this other verse was revealed concerning them: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they believe in it. And when it is recited to them, they say, "We believed in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims before it."﴾ Meaning: before this Qur'an we were Muslims, i.e., monotheists, sincerely devoted to Allah, submitting to Him.

Allah says: ﴿Those will be given their reward twice, for that they were patient﴾, i.e., those who possess this quality, who believed in the first Book and then in the second. They will be given their reward twice for their belief in the first Messenger and then in the second. Therefore He said: ﴿for that they were patient﴾, i.e., in following the truth, for such adherence is difficult upon the souls.

It has been reported in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of 'Amir al-Sha'bi, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three will be given their reward twice: a man from the People of the Book who believed in his prophet and then believed in me; a slave who fulfilled the right of Allah and the right of his masters; and a man who had a slave-girl whom he educated well, then freed her and married her."

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq al-Sayhani narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah who said: I was under the mount of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of the Conquest, and he said a fine and beautiful statement, and among what he said: "Whoever embraces Islam from among the People of the Two Books, he will have his reward twice, and he will have what we have and bear what we bear. And whoever embraces Islam from among the polytheists, he will have his reward, and he will have what we have and bear what we bear."

As for His saying ﴿and they repel evil with good﴾, i.e., they do not repay evil with its like, but rather they pardon and overlook. ﴿And from what We have provided them, they spend﴾, i.e., from what Allah has provided them of lawful sustenance they spend upon the creatures of Allah: in obligatory maintenance for their families and relatives, in obligatory zakat and recommended voluntary charity, and in supererogatory acts of charity and acts of drawing near to Allah.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And when they hear vain talk, they turn away from it﴾, i.e., they do not mix with its people nor associate with them, but rather, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when they pass by vain talk, they pass by with dignity﴾ [al-Furqan: 72].

﴿And they say, "To us our deeds, and to you your deeds. Peace be upon you. We do not seek the ignorant."﴾ i.e., when a foolish person acts foolishly toward them and speaks to them in a manner not worthy of reply, they turn away from him and do not respond to him with similar ugly speech, and nothing proceeds from them except good speech. Therefore He said of them that they said: ﴿To us our deeds and to you your deeds, peace be upon you, we do not seek the ignorant﴾, i.e., we do not desire the way of the ignorant nor love it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said in the Sirah: Then there came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while he was in Makkah, twenty men or about that number, from the Christians, when news of him had reached them from Abyssinia. They found him in the mosque, so they sat with him, spoke with him and questioned him, while men of Quraysh were in their assemblies around the Ka'bah. When they had finished questioning the Messenger of Allah about what they wanted, he invited them to Allah and recited the Qur'an to them. When they heard the Qur'an, their eyes overflowed with tears; then they responded to Allah, believed in him and affirmed him, and they recognized from him what had been described to them of his matter in their Book. When they rose from him, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham confronted them with a group of Quraysh, and they said to them: "May Allah disappoint you as a caravan! Those behind you from the people of your religion sent you to gather information for them, so that you might come to them with news of the man, but your gatherings were not at ease with him until you abandoned your religion and affirmed him in what he said. We know of no caravan more foolish than you." Or as they said to them. They replied: "Peace be upon you. We will not be ignorant toward you. To us is what we are upon, and to you is what you are upon. We did not fail to seek good for ourselves."

He said: It is said that the Christian group were from the people of Najran. Allah knows best which of these was the case.

He said: It is said, and Allah knows best, that these verses were revealed concerning them: ﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it, they believe in it﴾ up to His saying: ﴿We do not seek the ignorant﴾.

Al-Zuhri said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrated to me, from his father, who was al-Musayyab ibn Hazn al-Makhzumi, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: When death approached Abu Talib, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him and found with him Abu Jahl ibn Hisham and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O uncle, say: There is no god but Allah, a word by which I will testify for you before Allah." Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah said: "O Abu Talib, will you turn away from the religion of Abd al-Muttalib?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept presenting it to him, and they kept repeating that statement to him, until he said his last words: "He is upon the religion of Abd al-Muttalib," and he refused to say: "There is no god but Allah." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Allah, I will surely seek forgiveness for you, as long as I am not forbidden from doing so." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "It is not for the Prophet and those who believed to seek forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were close relatives" [Qur'an 9:113], and He revealed concerning Abu Talib: "Indeed, you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim reported it through the narration of al-Zuhri (Sahih al-Bukhari no. 1360 and Sahih Muslim no. 24).

Muslim in his Sahih, and al-Tirmidhi, reported it in the same way through the narration of Yazid ibn Kaysan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When the death of Abu Talib approached, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him and said: "O uncle, say: There is no god but Allah, I will testify for you by it on the Day of Resurrection." He said: "Were it not that Quraysh would reproach me for it, saying that only the fear of death made him (say it), I would have made your eye content by it. I will not say it except to make your eye content." Then Allah revealed: "Indeed, you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills, and He is most knowing of those who are guided." Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib; we do not know it except through the narration of Yazid ibn Kaysan" (Sahih Muslim no. 25 and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3188).

Imam Ahmad also narrated it from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, from Yazid ibn Kaysan, who said: Abu Hazim narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, and mentioned it in similar wording (Musnad, 2/434).

Thus Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Mujahid, al-Sha'bi and Qatadah said: It was revealed concerning Abu Talib when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked him to say: "There is no god but Allah," but he refused and said: "O nephew, (I follow) the religion of the elders." And his last words were: "He is upon the religion of Abd al-Muttalib."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Salamah narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, with his chain, from Sa'id ibn Abi Rashid, who said: A messenger of Caesar came to me (and) said: Caesar sent a letter with me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so I came to him and handed over the letter, and he placed it in his lap, then said: "What is the man's (lineage)?" I said: From Tanukh. He said: "Are you interested in the religion of your father Abraham, the Hanif?" I said: "I am a messenger of a people, and I will remain upon their religion until I return to them." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed, looked at his companions and said: "Indeed, you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills" (Musnad Ahmad, 3/441, through the route of Hammad ibn Salamah, similar in wording).

As for His saying: "And they say: If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched from our land" [Qur'an 28:57]: Almighty Allah informs about the excuse of some disbelievers for not following the guidance, when they said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched from our land." That is, they feared that if they followed what you brought of guidance and opposed those around them among the polytheistic Arab tribes, they would be targeted with harm and warfare, and would be snatched away wherever they were. So Allah, Exalted, answered them: "Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary?" meaning: this excuse they gave is a lie and falsehood, because Allah placed them in a secure land and a sacred, honored sanctuary, safe since it was established. How can this sanctuary be safe while they are in disbelief and polytheism, yet not safe for them when they have embraced Islam and followed the truth?

* *

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "It is not for the Prophet and those who believed to seek forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were close relatives" [Qur'an 9:113], and He revealed concerning Abu Talib: "Indeed, you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim reported it through the narration of al-Zuhri (Sahih al-Bukhari no. 1360 and Sahih Muslim no. 24).

Muslim in his Sahih, and al-Tirmidhi, reported it in the same way through the narration of Yazid ibn Kaysan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When the death of Abu Talib approached, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him and said: "O uncle, say: There is no god but Allah, I will testify for you by it on the Day of Resurrection." He said: "Were it not that Quraysh would reproach me for it, saying that only the fear of death made him (say it), I would have made your eye content by it. I will not say it except to make your eye content." Then Allah revealed: "Indeed, you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills, and He is most knowing of those who are guided." Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib; we do not know it except through the narration of Yazid ibn Kaysan" (Sahih Muslim no. 25 and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3188).

Imam Ahmad also narrated it from Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, from Yazid ibn Kaysan, who said: Abu Hazim narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, and mentioned it in similar wording (Musnad, 2/434).

Thus Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Mujahid, al-Sha'bi and Qatadah said: It was revealed concerning Abu Talib when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked him to say: "There is no god but Allah," but he refused and said: "O nephew, (I follow) the religion of the elders." And his last words were: "He is upon the religion of Abd al-Muttalib."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Salamah narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, with his chain, from Sa'id ibn Abi Rashid, who said: A messenger of Caesar came to me (and) said: Caesar sent a letter with me to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so I came to him and handed over the letter, and he placed it in his lap, then said: "What is the man's (lineage)?" I said: From Tanukh. He said: "Are you interested in the religion of your father Abraham, the Hanif?" I said: "I am a messenger of a people, and I will remain upon their religion until I return to them." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed, looked at his companions and said: "Indeed, you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah guides whom He wills" (Musnad Ahmad, 3/441, through the route of Hammad ibn Salamah, similar in wording).

* *

As for His saying: "And they say: If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched from our land" [Qur'an 28:57]: Almighty Allah informs about the excuse of some disbelievers for not following the guidance, when they said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched from our land." That is, they feared that if they followed what you brought of guidance and opposed those around them among the polytheistic Arab tribes, they would be targeted with harm and warfare, and would be snatched away wherever they were. So Allah, Exalted, answered them: "Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary?" meaning: this excuse they gave is a lie and falsehood, because Allah placed them in a secure land and a sacred, honored sanctuary, safe since it was established. How can this sanctuary be safe while they are in disbelief and polytheism, yet not safe for them when they have embraced Islam and followed the truth?

* *

As for His saying: "To which are brought the fruits of all things" [Qur'an 28:57], that is, the fruits of all kinds from what surrounds it, such as al-Ta'if and elsewhere, and likewise the merchandise and goods; "as a provision from Us" [Qur'an 28:57], that is, from Our side; "but most of them do not know" [Qur'an 28:57], and therefore they said what they said.

Al-Nasa'i said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me, who said: Amr ibn Shu'ayb said, from Ibn Abbas, and he did not hear it from him: That al-Harith ibn Amir ibn Nawfal is the one who said: "If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched from our land" (al-Nasa'i, al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11385).

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, addressing the people of Makkah by way of reproach, concerning His words: ﴿And how many a town have We destroyed which exulted in its livelihood﴾. That is: it transgressed, behaved insolently, and denied the blessing of Allah (نعم الله) in the provisions He had bestowed upon them, as He said in another verse: ﴿And Allah presents an example: a town that was secure and tranquil, its provision coming to it in abundance from every place, but it denied the favours of Allah, so Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear for what they used to do. And there had certainly come to them a Messenger from among themselves, but they denied him, so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers﴾ [An-Nahl 16:112–113]. And for this reason He said: ﴿Those are their dwellings, not inhabited after them except a little﴾. That is: their homes were obliterated, so you see nothing but their dwellings.

* *

And His words: ﴿And We were the inheritors﴾. That is: it returned to ruin, with no one in it.

Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned [here] from Ibn Mas'ud that he heard Ka'b saying to Umar: Indeed Sulayman (peace be upon him) said to the hoopoe, meaning the owl: "Why do you not eat the crops?" She said: "Because Adam was expelled from Paradise because of it." He said: "Why do you not drink water?" She said: "Because Allah drowned the people of Nuh with it." He said: "Why do you not dwell except in ruins?" She said: "Because it is the inheritance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic," then he recited: ﴿And We were the inheritors﴾.

Then Allah said, informing of His justice, and that He does not destroy anyone who is wronging Him, but He destroys only those whom He destroys after the establishment of the proof against them. And for this reason He said: ﴿And your Lord would never destroy the cities until He sends in their mother [city] a messenger reciting to them Our verses﴾, and she is Makkah. This indicates that the unlettered Prophet, who is Muhammad (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him), sent from Umm al-Qura, is a messenger to all the cities, of Arabs and non-Arabs (a'jam), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it﴾ [Ash-Shura 42:7]; and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾ [Al-A'raf 7:158]; and He said: ﴿That I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches﴾ [Al-An'am 6:19]; and He said: ﴿And whoever among the sects disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ [Hud 11:17]. The complete evidence is His words: ﴿And there is not a city but We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with a severe punishment. That was in the Book inscribed﴾ [Al-Isra 17:58]. So He informed that He would destroy every city before the Day of Resurrection, and He said: ﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾ [Al-Isra 17:15]. Thus Allah made the sending of the unlettered Prophet encompass all the cities, because he is sent to their mother and their origin to which they return.

And it is established in the Two Sahihs from him (may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him) that he said: "I have been sent to the red and the black." And for this reason He sealed prophethood and messengership with him, so there is no prophet after him and no messenger, rather his law remains as long as the night and day remain until the Day of Resurrection.

It was also said: the meaning of His words ﴿until He sends in its mother﴾ is: in its origin and its greatest city, like the mother cities of districts and regions. This was related by az-Zamakhshari, Ibn al-Jawzi, and others, and it is not far-fetched.

Allah, the Exalted, says, informing about the worthlessness of the worldly life, and the base adornment and fleeting splendor that it contains, in comparison with what Allah has prepared for His righteous servants in the Hereafter of great and lasting bliss, as He said: ﴿What is with you will perish, but what is with Allah is lasting﴾ [An-Nahl: 96]. He also said: ﴿And what is with Allah is better for the righteous﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 198]. He said: ﴿And the worldly life, in comparison with the Hereafter, is but a brief enjoyment﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 26]. He said: ﴿Rather, you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾ [Al-A'la: 16-17]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, the worldly life compared to the Hereafter is only like one of you dipping his finger into the sea; let him see what it brings back." [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. 2858, from the hadith of al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddad (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

[And His saying]: ﴿Will they not reason?﴾ [[In manuscripts F and A: "Will you not reason?"]] That is: will not one who prefers the worldly life over the Hereafter reason?

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Is one to whom We have promised a good promise, and he will meet it, like one whom We have given the enjoyment of the worldly life, then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forth?﴾ He means: Is one who is a believer, who affirms what Allah has promised for his good deeds of reward, to which he is certainly heading, like one who is a disbelieving denier of the meeting with Allah and of His promise and His threat? The latter is given enjoyment in the worldly life for a few days, ﴿then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forth﴾. Mujahid and Qatadah said: "Among those who will be punished."

Then it has been said that this verse was revealed concerning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Jahl. It was also said: concerning Hamzah, Ali and Abu Jahl. Both reports are from Mujahid. The apparent meaning is that it is general in application. This is like His saying, relating about that believer when he looked down upon his companion, while the believer is in the ranks of elevation and that one is in the depths of punishment: ﴿Had it not been for the grace of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forth﴾ [As-Saffat: 57]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the jinn have certainly known that they will be brought forth [to punishment]﴾ [As-Saffat: 158].

Allah says, describing what He will rebuke the disbelieving polytheists with on the Day of Resurrection, when He calls out to them and says: ﴿Where are My partners whom you used to claim?﴾

That is, where are the deities you used to worship in the worldly life, the idols and rivals? Can they help you, or can they defend themselves? This is said in the manner of reproach and threat, as He says: ﴿And you have certainly come to Us alone, as We created you the first time, and you have left behind you what We bestowed upon you. And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners [of Allah] among you. Your relations have been severed, and lost from you is what you used to claim﴾ [Al-An'am: 94].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Those about whom the Word has come into effect will say﴾, that is: from among the devils, the arrogant leaders, and the callers to disbelief, ﴿Our Lord, these are the ones we misguided. We misguided them as we ourselves were misguided. We disassociate ourselves before You. They did not used to worship us﴾. So they testify against them that they misled them and they followed them, and then they disown their worship of them, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And they have taken other than Allah as gods that they might be for them a source of honor. No! They will reject their worship of them and will be opposing them﴾ [Maryam: 81, 82]. And He says: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, one who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they, of their supplication, are unaware? And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 5, 6]. And Abraham said to his people: ﴿You have only taken idols instead of Allah as a bond of affection among you in the worldly life. Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will deny others and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and for you there will be no helpers﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 25]. And Allah says: ﴿When those who were followed disassociate themselves from those who followed, and they see the punishment, and their ties are cut off. And those who followed will say, "If only we had another return, we would disassociate ourselves from them as they have disassociated from us." Thus will Allah show them their deeds as regrets upon them, and they will never depart from the Fire﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 166, 167].

For this reason He says: ﴿And it will be said, "Call your partners"﴾, that is, to rescue you from what you are in, just as you used to hope from them in the worldly life. ﴿So they will call them, but they will not respond to them, and they will see the punishment﴾, that is, they will be certain that they are destined for the Fire without doubt.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿If only they had been guided﴾, that is, they will wish, when they witness the punishment, that they had been among the guided in the worldly life. This is like His saying: ﴿And the Day He will say, "Call your partners whom you claimed." So they will call them, but they will not respond to them, and We will place between them a barrier of destruction. And the criminals will see the Fire and will realize that they are to fall therein, and they will find no escape from it﴾ [Al-Kahf: 52, 53].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the Day He will call to them and say, "What was your response to the messengers?"﴾: the first call concerns the question of monotheism, and this includes the affirmation of prophethood: "What was your answer to the messengers sent to you? And how was your conduct with them?" This is like the servant being questioned in his grave: "Who is your Lord? Who is your Prophet? And what is your religion?" As for the believer, he testifies that there is no deity but Allah, and that Muhammad is the servant of Allah and His Messenger. As for the disbeliever, he says, "Hah... hah... I do not know." Therefore, on the Day of Resurrection he has no answer except silence, because whoever was blind in this world will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray in the path. For this reason Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then the information will be obscured from them that Day, and they will not question one another﴾.

Mujahid said: "The proofs will be obscured from them, so they will not ask one another about lineages."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿But as for one who repents and believes and does righteousness﴾, that is, in the worldly life, ﴿it is expected that he will be among the successful﴾.

That is, on the Day of Resurrection. And "expected" (ʿasā) from Allah is binding, for this will certainly come to pass by Allah's grace and bounty.

[[Following this in (T) and (F): "Chapter: Consider these verses and what they contain of lessons and evidence of Allah's lordship and wisdom, how He made the night a tranquility and a garment, covering the world, so that movements come to rest in it, animals return to their dens and birds to their nests, and souls are refreshed in it and relieved from the toil of striving and fatigue, until, when souls have taken their rest and steadiness from it, they look toward their livelihoods and their activities. Then comes the One who splits the dawn, glorified is He, with the day, and the herald of morning goes before Him, defeating that darkness and tearing it apart completely, removing it and uncovering it from the world, so that they are seeing. Animals spread out and go about their livelihoods and affairs, and birds leave their nests. How wondrous is that promise! It is a beginning that points to Allah's power over the great Return, and its repetition and the souls' witnessing of it, to the point that it has become a habit and something familiar, has prevented them from taking heed and reasoning from it toward the second creation and the revival of creatures after their death. The Sunnah has indeed reported this: that the servant is answered when he rises from his sleep and says: 'All praise is due to Allah, who gave us life after our death, and to Him is the resurrection.'"]].

﴿And We will extract from every nation a witness.﴾ Mujahid said: this means a messenger. ﴿Then We will say, "Produce your proof."﴾ That is, to establish the truth of what you claimed, that Allah has partners. ﴿Then they will know that the truth belongs to Allah.﴾ That is, there is no god besides Him. Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 28, verse 76–77:

Al-A'mash narrated from Al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said regarding ﴿Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Musa﴾: "He was his paternal cousin." Likewise said Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, Simak ibn Harb, Qatadah, Malik ibn Dinar, Ibn Jurayj and others: that he was a cousin of Musa, peace be upon him [[In T: "peace and blessings of Allah be upon him".]].

Ibn Jurayj said: He is Qarun ibn Yashhar ibn Qahith, and Musa ibn 'Imran ibn Qahith.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar claimed that Qarun was the paternal uncle of Musa, peace be upon him [[In F and A: "Musa ibn 'Imran".]].

Ibn Jarir said: Most of the scholars hold that he was his cousin, and Allah knows best. Qatadah ibn Di'amah said: We used to be told that he was a cousin of Musa, and he was called "al-Munawwar" (the Illuminated) for the beauty of his voice in reciting the Torah. But the enemy of Allah became a hypocrite just as al-Samiri did, and rebellion destroyed him because of the abundance of his wealth.

Shahr ibn Hawshab said: He lengthened his garments by a span, out of arrogance towards his people.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And We gave him of the treasures﴾, meaning of the wealth, ﴿such that its keys would indeed burden a band of strong men﴾, meaning their load would weigh down a great number of people because of their abundance.

Al-A'mash narrated from Khaythamah: The keys to Qarun's treasures were of leather, each key the size of a finger, and each key was for a separate chest. When he rode, they were loaded onto sixty white-blazed mules. It was also said other than this, and Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying ﴿When his people said to him, "Do not exult; indeed Allah does not love the exultant"﴾, meaning: they admonished him regarding what he was in, advising him for his own good, saying by way of counsel and guidance: "Do not exult in what you have", meaning: do not be insolent with the wealth you possess. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: meaning the boastful (al-Marihin). Mujahid said: meaning the haughty and insolent, who do not thank Allah for what He has given them.

* *

As for His saying ﴿But seek, through what Allah has given you, the Home of the Hereafter, and do not forget your share of the world﴾, meaning: use what Allah has bestowed upon you of this abundant wealth and great blessing in obedience to your Lord and in drawing near to Him through various acts of worship, by which you will gain reward in the Hereafter. ﴿And do not forget your share of the world﴾, meaning: of what Allah has permitted in it of food, drink, clothing, housing and marriage, for your Lord has a right over you, your self has a right over you, your family has a right over you, and your visitor has a right over you, so give every rightful person his right.

﴿And do good as Allah has done good to you﴾, meaning: do good to His creation as He has done good to you. ﴿And do not seek corruption in the land﴾, meaning: let not your aspiration in what you have be to corrupt the land with it and harm the creatures of Allah. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters.﴾

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah, the Exalted, says, reporting the reply of Qarun to his people when they advised him and guided him toward goodness: ﴿He said, "I have only been given it on account of knowledge I possess."﴾ That is: I have no need for what you say, for Allah, the Exalted, has given me this wealth only because He knows that I deserve it, and out of His love for me. Its meaning is: I was given it because of Allah's knowledge that I am worthy of it. This is like His saying, ﴿So when harm touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a favour from Us, he says, "I have only been given it on account of knowledge."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 49] That is, on knowledge from Allah about me. And like His saying, ﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after some hardship has touched him, he will surely say, "This is mine (by right)."﴾ [Fussilat: 50] That is, "This is what I deserve."

It has been narrated from some of them that he meant: ﴿I have only been given it on account of knowledge I possess﴾ — that he was practising the science of alchemy. This view is weak, because alchemy in itself is a false science, since transmuting substances is something no one can do except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Allah says: ﴿O mankind, a parable has been presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those whom you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it﴾ [Al-Hajj: 73]. And in the Sahih it is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Allah, the Exalted, says: 'Who is more unjust than one who attempts to create like My creation? Let them create an atom, or let them create a grain of barley.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5953; Sahih Muslim, no. 2111.] This was said concerning the image-makers who imitate Allah's creation merely in outward form or shape, so how much more so for one who claims that he can transform the essence of this substance into the essence of another substance. This is falsehood and impossibility, ignorance and misguidance. They are only able to apply colouring to the outward appearance, which is a lie, adulteration and deception, and a promotion of the claim that it is genuine in reality, when it is certainly not so. It has never been established by any lawful means that anyone succeeded through this method which these ignorant, corrupt, lying deceivers practise. As for what Allah, the Exalted, brings about through the breaking of customary patterns at the hands of some of the saints, transforming some substances into gold or silver or the like, this is a matter that no Muslim denies and no believer rejects. But this is not of the category of crafts; rather, it is by the will of the Lord of the earth and the heavens, His choice and His action. It is narrated of Haywah ibn Shurayh al-Misri, may Allah have mercy on him, that a questioner asked him for something, but he had nothing to give him, and he saw his need, so he took a pebble from the ground, rolled it around in his palm, then threw it to that questioner, and behold, it was red gold. The narrations and reports on this are very numerous, too lengthy to mention.

Some of them said: Qarun knew the Greatest Name (al-Ism al-A'zam) of Allah, so he invoked Allah with it, and thereby became wealthy. The correct view is the first meaning. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, said, refuting him in what he claimed regarding Allah's concern for him in what He gave him of wealth: ﴿Did he not know that Allah had already destroyed before him generations who were greater than him in strength and more abundant in accumulation?﴾ That is: there were those who were more wealthy than him, and that was not out of any love from Us for them; and Allah destroyed them nonetheless because of their disbelief and their failure to be grateful. Therefore He said: ﴿And the criminals will not be asked about their sins﴾, that is, because of the multitude of their sins.

Qatadah said: ﴿on account of knowledge I possess﴾: "on account of goodness that is with me."

As-Suddi said: "On account of knowledge that I am worthy of that."

And the Imam Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam excelled in the interpretation of this verse. He said concerning His saying, ﴿He said, "I have only been given it on account of knowledge I possess."﴾: "Were it not for Allah's pleasure with me, and His knowledge of my merit, He would not have given me this wealth." And he recited: ﴿Did he not know that Allah had already destroyed before him generations who were greater than him in strength and more abundant in accumulation? And the criminals will not be asked about their sins.﴾ [And this is how one of little knowledge speaks: when he sees someone whom Allah has granted abundance, he says, "Were he not deserving of that, he would not have been given it."]

The Exalted says, informing about Qarun: One day he went out to his people in great finery and splendid adornment, with mounts and garments, both he and his attendants and retinue. When those who desire the worldly life and incline toward its glitter and adornment saw him, they wished that they had the like of what he had been given. They said: "Oh, if only we had the like of what Qarun has been given. Indeed, he is one of great fortune." That is, he has a generous share of the world. When the people of beneficial knowledge heard their words, they said to them: "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds." That is, Allah's recompense for His righteous, believing servants in the Hereafter is better than what you see.

[As in the sound hadith: Allah the Exalted says: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." And recite, if you wish: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes, as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [As-Sajdah: 17] [[Addition from manuscripts T, F, A.]] [[Sahih Muslim, no. 2824.]].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿But none is granted it except the patient﴾: Al-Suddi said: "And none is granted Paradise except the patient." It seems he took this as part of the speech of those who were given knowledge. Ibn Jarir said: "And none is granted this statement except the patient, who restrain themselves from loving the world and who desire the Hereafter." It seems he took it as separate from the speech of those people, and considered it part of the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His informing of that.
