Commentary of Ibn Kathir (*Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*) on Surah 28, verses 81–82:

When the Exalted mentioned Qarun's arrogance in his adornment, his boasting over his people, and his oppression of them, He followed this with the fact that He caused the earth to swallow him and his home, as is established in the *Sahih* (in al-Bukhari, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Salim) that his father told him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "While a man was dragging his lower garment, he was swallowed up [[In the variant text (ت): "Allah caused him to be swallowed up."]], and he will keep sinking into the earth until the Day of Resurrection."

Then he narrated it through the hadith of Jarir ibn Zayd, from Salim, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with similar wording [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5790.]].

Imam Ahmad said: Al-Nadr ibn Isma'il Abu al-Mughirah al-Qass narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "While a man among those who came before you went out wearing two green cloaks, strutting in them, Allah commanded the earth and it seized him, and he will keep sinking into it until the Day of Resurrection." Ahmad alone related it [[Al-Musnad (3/40)]], and its chain is *hasan* (good) [[In the variant text (ت): "Ahmad related it with his chain."]] [[In the variant text (ت): "The Prophet."]].

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Abu Khaythamah narrated to us, Abu Mu'alla ibn Mansur narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Muslim informed me, I heard Ziyad al-Numayri narrating from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "While a man among those who came before you went out in two cloaks and strutted in them, Allah commanded the earth and it seized him, and he will keep sinking into it until the Day of Resurrection." [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/279). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (5/126): "In its chain is Ziyad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Numayri, who is weak. Ibn Hibban regarded him as trustworthy but said he makes mistakes."]] [[In the variant texts (ف، أ): "Mimman" instead of "Fiman."]]

Muhammad ibn al-Mundhir [[In the variant text (ت، ف، أ): the word "al-Hafiz" is inserted here.]] mentioned in his book *al-'Aja'ib al-Gharibah*, with his chain, from Nawfal ibn Musahiq, who said: I saw a young man in the mosque of Najran, and I kept looking at him and marveling at his height, completeness, and beauty. He said: "Why are you looking at me?" I said: "I marvel at your beauty and perfection." He said: "Indeed, Allah marvels at me." He said: "He continued to diminish and diminish until he became the height of a span. Then one of his relatives took him in his sleeve and departed."

It has been mentioned that the destruction of Qarun was in response to the supplication of the Prophet of Allah Musa (peace be upon him) [[In the variant text (ت): "peace and blessings of Allah be upon him."]], and there is disagreement about its cause. From Ibn 'Abbas and al-Suddi: Qarun gave a prostitute wealth on condition that she accuse Musa, in the presence of the assembly of the Children of Israel, while he was standing among them reciting the Book of Allah, of having done such-and-such to her. When she said this in front of the assembly to Musa (peace be upon him), he trembled with fear. He turned to her, prayed two units of prayer, and then said: "I adjure you by Allah, who split the sea and delivered you from Pharaoh, and did such-and-such and such-and-such, to tell me what moved you to say what you said." She said: "Since you have adjured me, Qarun gave me such-and-such on condition that I say this to you. I seek Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him." At that, Musa fell down prostrate to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and asked Allah concerning Qarun. Allah revealed to him: "I have commanded the earth to obey you concerning him." So Musa commanded the earth to swallow him and his house, and it happened.

It was also said: When Qarun went out to his people in that adornment, riding white mules, with himself and his attendants wearing crimson dyed garments [[In the variant texts (ت، ف، أ): "the dyed garments."]], he passed with that entourage by the gathering of the Prophet of Allah Musa (peace be upon him), who was reminding them of the Days of Allah. When people saw Qarun, the faces of the people turned toward him, looking at what he had. Musa (peace be upon him) called him and said: "What moved you to do what you did?" He said: "O Musa, as for your being favored over me with prophethood, I have been favored over you with worldly wealth. If you wish, let us go out and you supplicate against me and I supplicate against you." So they went out, and Qarun went out with his people. Musa said: "Will you supplicate or shall I?" He said: "No, I will supplicate." Qarun supplicated, but it was not answered for him. Then Musa said: "Shall I supplicate?" He said: "Yes." Musa said: "O Allah, command the earth to obey me today." Allah revealed to him: "I have done so." Musa said: "O earth, seize them." It seized them up to their feet. Then he said: "Seize them." It seized them up to their knees, then to their shoulders. Then he said: "Bring forth their treasures and wealth." So it brought them forth until they looked at them. Then Musa pointed with his hand and said: "Go, O sons of Lawi [[In the variant text (أ): "Go with him, I do not see [him]."]]." So the earth closed over them.

It is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: They were swallowed into the seventh earth.

Qatadah said: It has been related to us that every day they are swallowed a man's height deeper, and they will keep sinking therein until the Day of Resurrection.

Here there are strange *Isra'iliyyat* (narratives from Jewish and Christian sources) [[In the variant texts (ت، ف): "strange" is inserted.]], which we have turned away from entirely.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So he had no party to help him against Allah, nor was he among those who could defend themselves.﴾ That is: his wealth did not avail him, nor did what he had gathered, nor his servants and retinue. Neither did they repel from him the vengeance of Allah, His punishment, and His retribution [[In the variant text (أ): "upon him" is inserted.]]. Nor was he himself able to defend himself, so he had no helper from himself or from anyone else [[In the variant text (أ): "not" is inserted.]].

* *

As for the Exalted's saying: ﴿And those who had wished to be in his place the day before began to say...﴾ That is: those who, when they saw him in his adornment, said: ﴿Oh, if only we had the like of what Qarun has been given! Indeed, he is of great fortune.﴾ When he was swallowed up, they began to say: ﴿Ah, it seems that Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it.﴾ That is: wealth is not a sign of Allah's pleasure with its owner [[In the variant text (أ): "and His servants" is inserted.]]. For Allah gives and withholds, constricts and expands, lowers and raises, and His is perfect wisdom and conclusive proof. This is like what is in the *marfu'* hadith from Ibn Mas'ud: "Indeed, Allah has divided among you your characters just as He has divided your provisions. Allah gives wealth to whom He loves and to whom He does not love, but He gives faith only to the one He loves" [[Al-Musnad (1/387).]].

﴿Had Allah not been gracious to us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us.﴾ That is: had Allah's kindness to us and His beneficence toward us not been, He would have caused the earth to swallow us as He swallowed him, because we had wished to be like him.

﴿Ah, it seems the disbelievers do not prosper.﴾ They mean: he was a disbeliever, and the disbeliever does not prosper before Allah, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.

The grammarians have differed about the meaning of the Exalted's saying here [[In the variant texts (ت، ف، أ): "here" is inserted.]]: ﴿wayka'anna﴾. Some of them said its meaning is: "Woe to you, know that..." but it was lightened, so it became "wayka," and the opening of "anna" indicates the deletion of "i'lam" (know). This view was weakened by Ibn Jarir [[Tafsir al-Tabari (20/77).]], though it appears strong. The only difficulty for it is that it is written in the mushafs as one connected word, "wayka'anna." But writing is a conventional, customary matter, and the reference is to the Arabic pronunciation. And Allah knows best.

It was also said: its meaning is "wayka'anna," i.e., "Did you not see that...?" This was said by Qatadah. It was also said that its meaning is "wayka" separated, with "way" being a particle of wonder or alerting, and "ka'anna" meaning "I think and I suppose." Ibn Jarir said: The strongest of these views is Qatadah's statement that it means: "Did you not see that...?" and he cited the words of the poet [[He is Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl, and the verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (20/77).]]:

*"Two women asked me for divorce when they saw me, my wealth diminished, and you two had come to me with a denial..."*

*"Ah, it seems that whoever has wealth is praised, and whoever is poor lives a life of hardship..."*

Muhammad ibn al-Mundhir [[In the variant text (ت، ف، أ): the word "al-Hafiz" is inserted here.]] mentioned in his book *al-'Aja'ib al-Gharibah*, with his chain, from Nawfal ibn Musahiq, who said: I saw a young man in the mosque of Najran, and I kept looking at him and marveling at his height, completeness, and beauty. He said: "Why are you looking at me?" I said: "I marvel at your beauty and perfection." He said: "Indeed, Allah marvels at me." He said: "He continued to diminish and diminish until he became the height of a span. Then one of his relatives took him in his sleeve and departed."

It has been mentioned that the destruction of Qarun was in response to the supplication of the Prophet of Allah Musa (peace be upon him) [[In the variant text (ت): "peace and blessings of Allah be upon him."]], and there is disagreement about its cause. From Ibn 'Abbas and al-Suddi: Qarun gave a prostitute wealth on condition that she accuse Musa, in the presence of the assembly of the Children of Israel, while he was standing among them reciting the Book of Allah, of having done such-and-such to her. When she said this in front of the assembly to Musa (peace be upon him), he trembled with fear. He turned to her, prayed two units of prayer, and then said: "I adjure you by Allah, who split the sea and delivered you from Pharaoh, and did such-and-such and such-and-such, to tell me what moved you to say what you said." She said: "Since you have adjured me, Qarun gave me such-and-such on condition that I say this to you. I seek Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him." At that, Musa fell down prostrate to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and asked Allah concerning Qarun. Allah revealed to him: "I have commanded the earth to obey you concerning him." So Musa commanded the earth to swallow him and his house, and it happened.

It was also said: When Qarun went out to his people in that adornment, riding white mules, with himself and his attendants wearing crimson dyed garments [[In the variant texts (ت، ف، أ): "the dyed garments."]], he passed with that entourage by the gathering of the Prophet of Allah Musa (peace be upon him), who was reminding them of the Days of Allah. When people saw Qarun, the faces of the people turned toward him, looking at what he had. Musa (peace be upon him) called him and said: "What moved you to do what you did?" He said: "O Musa, as for your being favored over me with prophethood, I have been favored over you with worldly wealth. If you wish, let us go out and you supplicate against me and I supplicate against you." So they went out, and Qarun went out with his people. Musa said: "Will you supplicate or shall I?" He said: "No, I will supplicate." Qarun supplicated, but it was not answered for him. Then Musa said: "Shall I supplicate?" He said: "Yes." Musa said: "O Allah, command the earth to obey me today." Allah revealed to him: "I have done so." Musa said: "O earth, seize them." It seized them up to their feet. Then he said: "Seize them." It seized them up to their knees, then to their shoulders. Then he said: "Bring forth their treasures and wealth." So it brought them forth until they looked at them. Then Musa pointed with his hand and said: "Go, O sons of Lawi [[In the variant text (أ): "Go with him, I do not see [him]."]]." So the earth closed over them.

It is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: They were swallowed into the seventh earth.

Qatadah said: It has been related to us that every day they are swallowed a man's height deeper, and they will keep sinking therein until the Day of Resurrection.

Here there are strange *Isra'iliyyat* (narratives from Jewish and Christian sources) [[In the variant texts (ت، ف): "strange" is inserted.]], which we have turned away from entirely.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So he had no party to help him against Allah, nor was he among those who could defend themselves.﴾ That is: his wealth did not avail him, nor did what he had gathered, nor his servants and retinue. Neither did they repel from him the vengeance of Allah, His punishment, and His retribution [[In the variant text (أ): "upon him" is inserted.]]. Nor was he himself able to defend himself, so he had no helper from himself or from anyone else [[In the variant text (أ): "not" is inserted.]].

* *

As for the Exalted's saying: ﴿And those who had wished to be in his place the day before began to say...﴾ That is: those who, when they saw him in his adornment, said: ﴿Oh, if only we had the like of what Qarun has been given! Indeed, he is of great fortune.﴾ When he was swallowed up, they began to say: ﴿Ah, it seems that Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it.﴾ That is: wealth is not a sign of Allah's pleasure with its owner [[In the variant text (أ): "and His servants" is inserted.]]. For Allah gives and withholds, constricts and expands, lowers and raises, and His is perfect wisdom and conclusive proof. This is like what is in the *marfu'* hadith from Ibn Mas'ud: "Indeed, Allah has divided among you your characters just as He has divided your provisions. Allah gives wealth to whom He loves and to whom He does not love, but He gives faith only to the one He loves" [[Al-Musnad (1/387).]].

﴿Had Allah not been gracious to us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us.﴾ That is: had Allah's kindness to us and His beneficence toward us not been, He would have caused the earth to swallow us as He swallowed him, because we had wished to be like him.

﴿Ah, it seems the disbelievers do not prosper.﴾ They mean: he was a disbeliever, and the disbeliever does not prosper before Allah, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.

The grammarians have differed about the meaning of the Exalted's saying here [[In the variant texts (ت، ف، أ): "here" is inserted.]]: ﴿wayka'anna﴾. Some of them said its meaning is: "Woe to you, know that..." but it was lightened, so it became "wayka," and the opening of "anna" indicates the deletion of "i'lam" (know). This view was weakened by Ibn Jarir [[Tafsir al-Tabari (20/77).]], though it appears strong. The only difficulty for it is that it is written in the mushafs as one connected word, "wayka'anna." But writing is a conventional, customary matter, and the reference is to the Arabic pronunciation. And Allah knows best.

It was also said: its meaning is "wayka'anna," i.e., "Did you not see that...?" This was said by Qatadah. It was also said that its meaning is "wayka" separated, with "way" being a particle of wonder or alerting, and "ka'anna" meaning "I think and I suppose." Ibn Jarir said: The strongest of these views is Qatadah's statement that it means: "Did you not see that...?" and he cited the words of the poet [[He is Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl, and the verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (20/77).]]:

*"Two women asked me for divorce when they saw me, my wealth diminished, and you two had come to me with a denial..."*

*"Ah, it seems that whoever has wealth is praised, and whoever is poor lives a life of hardship..."*

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 28, verses 83–84:

Allah, may He be exalted, informs us that the Final Abode and its lasting bliss, which neither changes nor passes away, He has assigned to His believing servants who are humble, "those who do not desire haughtiness (*'uluww*) on the earth," that is, exalting themselves over the creation of Allah, magnifying themselves over them, and tyrannizing them, "nor corruption." As 'Ikrimah said: *al-'Uluww* is *al-tajabbur* (tyranny).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: *al-'Uluww* is *al-baghy* (oppression).

Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri narrated from Mansur, from Muslim al-Batin [[In A: "Salim".]]: *al-'Uluww fi'l-ard* is arrogance without right. And *al-fasad* is taking wealth without right.

Ibn Jurayj said: "*La yuridūna 'uluwwan fi'l-ard*" means magnifying oneself and tyrannizing, "*wa la fasadan*" means acting in acts of disobedience.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn WakI' narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ash'ath al-Sammān [[In A: "Ash'ab al-Sammak".]], from Abu Salam al-A'raj, from 'Ali, who said: "A man may be pleased that the strap of his sandal is finer than his companion's strap, and so he enters into the words of Allah: *'That is the Final Abode; We assign it to those who do not desire haughtiness on the earth or corruption, and the good end is for the righteous.'*"

This is to be understood as applying when a person intends by it boasting and showing superiority over others, for that is blameworthy, as is established in the Sahih, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "It has been revealed to me that you should be humble, so that no one boasts over another and no one oppresses another." [Sahih Muslim, no. 2865, from 'Iyad ibn Himar (may Allah be pleased with him).] As for loving that merely for beautification, there is no harm in it. It is established that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I love that my garment be fine and my sandal be fine. Is that pride?" He said: "No. Indeed Allah is beautiful and loves beauty."

And His saying: *"Whoever comes with a good deed, for him is better than it,"* that is, on the Day of Resurrection, *"better than it"* means Allah's reward is better than the servant's good deed. How much more so when Allah multiplies it many times over. This is the station of grace (*al-fadl*).

Then He said: *"And whoever comes with an evil deed, those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except with what they used to do,"* as He said in another verse: *"And whoever comes with an evil deed, their faces will be thrown into the Fire. Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?"* [al-Naml: 90]. This is the station of justice and fairness (*al-fasl wa'l-'adl*).

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 28, verses 85–88:

Allah, the Exalted, says, commanding His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, to convey the message and recite the Qur'an to the people, and informing him that He will return him to a return (ma'ad), which is the Day of Resurrection, where He will ask him about the burdens of prophethood entrusted to him. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, He who has ordained the Qur'an for you will surely bring you back to a return.﴾ That is: He has made it obligatory upon you to deliver it to the people. ﴿Will surely bring you back to a return﴾: that is, to the Day of Resurrection, where He will ask you about that, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers﴾ [Al-A'raf: 6], and He said: ﴿The Day when Allah will gather the messengers and say, "What was your response?" They will say, "We have no knowledge. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen."﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 109] [And He said]: [[Addition from manuscript T, A.]] ﴿And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought forward﴾ [Az-Zumar: 69].

Al-Suddi said, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed, He who has ordained the Qur'an for you will surely bring you back to a return﴾ – he said: "He will bring you back to Paradise, then He will question you about the Qur'an." Al-Suddi said: Abu Sa'id said the same.

al-Hakam ibn Aban said, from 'Ikrimah, [and] from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: ﴿will surely bring you back to a return﴾ – he said: "To the Day of Resurrection." Malik narrated it from al-Zuhri.

al-Thawri said, from al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿will surely bring you back to a return﴾: "To death."

There are several chains from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and in some of them: "He will bring you back to your origin (ma'din) in Paradise."

Mujahid said: "He will give you life on the Day of Resurrection." It was similarly narrated from 'Ikrimah, 'Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Qaza'ah, Abu Malik, and Abu Salih.

al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Yes, by Allah, indeed for him there is a return. Allah will resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection, then will admit him into Paradise."

Other than this has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, as al-Bukhari said in the Tafsir section of his Sahih:

Muhammad ibn Muqatil narrated to us, Ya'la informed us, Sufyan al-'Usfuri narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿will surely bring you back to a return﴾ – he said: "To Makkah."

Al-Nasa'i narrated it likewise in the Tafsir of his Sunan, and Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) narrated it from the hadith of Ya'la – he is Ibn 'Ubayd al-Tanafisi – with the same chain. [[al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11386), and Tafsir al-Tabari (20/80).]] Likewise al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿will surely bring you back to a return﴾, i.e., "will surely bring you back to Makkah, just as He brought you out of it."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿will surely bring you back to a return﴾: "To your birthplace, Makkah."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Atiyyah, and al-Dahhak, something similar to that.

[Our father narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, saying: Sufyan said: "We heard it from Muqatil seventy years ago, from al-Dahhak"] [[Addition from manuscripts F, A.]] he said: When the Prophet ﷺ left Makkah and reached al-Juhfah, he longed for Makkah, so Allah revealed to him: ﴿Indeed, He who has ordained the Qur'an for you will surely bring you back to a return﴾ – "to Makkah."

This statement of al-Dahhak implies that this verse is Medinan, although the whole surah is Meccan. And Allah knows best.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿will surely bring you back to a return﴾, he said: "This is among what Ibn 'Abbas used to conceal." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain from Nu'aym al-Qari that he said regarding His saying: ﴿will surely bring you back to a return﴾: "To Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem)."

This – and Allah knows best – goes back to the view of those who interpreted it as the Day of Resurrection, because Bayt al-Maqdis is the land of the gathering and the assembly. And Allah is the One who grants success to what is correct.

The way to reconcile these statements is that Ibn 'Abbas interpreted it at one time as his return to Makkah, which was the conquest that, according to Ibn 'Abbas, was a sign of the approach of the Prophet's appointed time, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him [[In manuscript A: "The appointed time of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace."]], just as Ibn 'Abbas interpreted by the surah ﴿When the victory of Allah has come and the conquest, and you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes, then exalt with praise of your Lord and seek His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾ [An-Nasr: 1–3], that it was the appointed time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ being announced to him, and that was in the presence of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and 'Umar agreed with him on that and said: "I know nothing of it except what you know." For this reason Ibn 'Abbas at another time interpreted His saying: ﴿will surely bring you back to a return﴾ as death, and at another time as the Day of Resurrection, which comes after death, and at another time as Paradise, which is his reward and final destination for conveying the message of Allah and delivering it to the two worlds, jinn and mankind, and because he is the most perfect of Allah's creation, the most eloquent of Allah's creation, and the most noble of Allah's creation without qualification.

* *

His saying: ﴿Say, "My Lord knows best who has come with guidance and who is in clear error."﴾ That is: Say – to those who opposed you and denied you, O Muhammad, from your people, among the polytheists and those who followed them in their disbelief – say: "My Lord knows best who among you and among me is rightly guided." And you will know whose will be the final outcome of the abode, and to whom the final outcome and victory will belong, in this world and the Hereafter.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said, reminding His Prophet of His great blessing upon him and upon the servants in sending him to them: ﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you﴾ – that is: you did not think, before the revelation was sent down to you, that revelation would descend upon you. ﴿But it was a mercy from your Lord﴾ – that is: revelation was only sent down upon you from Allah out of His mercy toward you and toward the servants through you. So when He has granted you this great blessing, ﴿then never be a supporter for the disbelievers﴾ – that is: a helper to them. Rather, separate from them, renounce them, and oppose them.

﴿And let them not turn you away from the verses of Allah after they have been revealed to you﴾ – that is: do not be affected by their opposition to you and their hindering of people from your path; do not turn to that or care about it. For Allah will exalt your word, support your religion, and make manifest what you were sent with over all other religions. For this reason He said: ﴿And invite to your Lord﴾ – that is: to the worship of your Lord alone, without partner – ﴿and never be among the polytheists.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not invoke with Allah another deity. There is no deity except Him﴾ – that is: worship is fitting only for Him, and divinity is appropriate only for His greatness.

* *

His saying: ﴿Everything will perish except His face﴾ – this is information that He is the Ever-Lasting, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, whom creatures die and He does not die, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Everyone upon it will perish. And there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honour﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 26–27]. So He expressed by "face" the Essence, and likewise His saying here: ﴿Everything will perish except His face﴾ – that is: except Him.

It is established in the Sahih, through the chain of Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The truest word a poet has ever spoken is the word of Labid:

"Surely everything other than Allah is vain." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3841), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2256).]]

Mujahid and al-Thawri said regarding His saying: ﴿Everything will perish except His face﴾: "That is: except what is intended by His face." Al-Bukhari related it in his Sahih as if affirming it.

Ibn Jarir said: Those who hold this view cite the words of the poet:

"I seek forgiveness from Allah for a sin I cannot count,
Lord of the servants, to Him are the face and the deed..."

This view does not contradict the first view, for this is information that all deeds are vain except those intended for the face of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, from the righteous deeds that conform to the Shari'ah. The first view implies that all essences are perishing, destroyed, and passing away except His Essence, the Exalted, for He is the First and the Last, who is before everything and after everything.

Abu Bakr 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Dunya said in his book "Al-Tafakkur wa al-I'tibar": Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr narrated to us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, 'Umar ibn Sulaym al-Bahili narrated to us, Abu al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Umar, whenever he wanted to examine his heart, would come to the ruin, stand at its door, call out in a sorrowful voice, and say: "Where are your people?" Then he would return to himself and say: ﴿Everything will perish except His face.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿To Him belongs the judgment﴾ – that is: dominion and disposal, and there is none to repel His command. ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾ – that is: on the day of your return, and He will recompense you for your deeds: if good, then good; and if evil, then evil.

[And Allah knows best. End of the tafsir of Surat al-Qasas]
